| `Scopes` | `[]AccessScope` | `{URI, Kind}`, ordered by URI. `Kind` is `permio.ScopeSubtree`, `ScopePattern`, `ScopeExact` (reserved, not returned today) or `ScopeUnknown` (a kind this SDK version doesn't know; it never matches). |
| `IsEmpty()` | `bool` | No access anywhere under `Under`. |
| `Allows(uri)` | `bool` | Whether `uri` is covered. Matches per segment: `/a/b` covers `/a/b/c` but not `/a/bc`. Malformed URIs are never allowed. |
| `Prefixes()` | `[]string` | The subtree URIs, for prefix filters. Prefixes covered by a shorter one are dropped. Pattern scopes aren't included. |
| `Patterns()` | `[]string` | The pattern URIs, with `_` segments. |
| `HasPatterns()` | `bool` | Some scope is a pattern, so `Prefixes()` alone doesn't cover everything. |
| `Exact()` | `[]string` | The exact URIs. Empty today. |
| `RegexpSource()` | `string` | One anchored regular expression matching exactly what `Allows` accepts, in syntax common to RE2, PCRE and POSIX ERE, so usable in PostgreSQL `~` and MongoDB `$regex`. Matches nothing when there are no scopes. |
| `Regexp()` | `*regexp.Regexp` | `RegexpSource()`, compiled. |

**Warning**

A prefix `p` from `Prefixes()` means `p` **and everything below it**. Filter with
`path = p OR path starts with p + "/"`, never a bare "starts with `p`", which would let `/documents/1` match
`/documents/12`. In SQL, use `starts_with(path, p || '/')` rather than `LIKE`, where `_` is a wildcard.

For a URI outside `Under`, `Allows` returning `false` means "not asked", not "denied". The API key needs
`permission.check` on `under` and `principal.assignment.get` on the principal.

#### `WhoHasAccess`

Answers "who has access to this resource?" (the `ListPrincipalsWithAccess` RPC). It follows every page and returns
an `[]AccessEntry`, ordered by principal ID. The options may be `nil`:

```go
entries, err := client.WhoHasAccess(ctx, "/documents/42", &permio.WhoHasAccessOptions{
    Permission:   "document.read",
    ExpandGroups: true,
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
// [
//   {Principal: "alice", Via: [{Resource: "/documents", Inherited: true, Match: "ancestor",
//                               Source: "role", RoleID: "ROLE_ID", RoleName: "viewer"}]},
//   {Principal: "bob", ViaGroup: "editors", Via: [...]},
//   {Principal: "group:editors", IsGroup: true, Via: [...]},
// ]
```

`WhoHasAccessOptions`:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Permission` | Only count grants that confer this permission, so a principal is listed exactly when a check passes for it through its own grants (or, for entries with `ViaGroup`, through that group). Empty: any grant counts. |
| `ExpandGroups` | Also list every member of each listed group, once per group, with `ViaGroup` set. |

`AccessEntry` has `Principal`, `IsGroup`, `ViaGroup` (a group slug, or `""`) and `Via`, the grants that give the
access, most specific first. Each `AccessVia` has:

- `Resource`: the URI the grant was made on (the resource, an ancestor, or a `_` wildcard URI that matches it);
- `Inherited`: `true` unless the grant was made on exactly the resource;
- `Match`: `"exact"`, `"ancestor"`, `"wildcard"` or `"unknown"`;
- `Source`: `"role"` (with `RoleID` and `RoleName`), `"direct"` for directly granted permissions, or `"unknown"`.

The API key needs `principal.list` and `principal.assignment.list` on the project.

### Granting and revoking

Grants and revokes need a key with full access. See [API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels).

```go
err := client.Grant(ctx, permio.GrantRequest{
    Principal:   "alice",
    Resource:    "/documents",          // also covers everything below it
    Permissions: []string{"document.read"},
    Roles:       []string{roleID},      // role IDs, not names
})

err = client.Revoke(ctx, permio.GrantRequest{
    Principal: "alice",
    Resource:  "/documents",
    Roles:     []string{roleID},
})
```

`GrantRequest` has `Principal`, `Resource`, `Permissions` (permission names) and `Roles` (role IDs). It needs at
least one permission or role.

- `Grant` is additive: what the principal already holds there is kept. Unknown permissions or roles fail with
  `KindValidation`.
- `Revoke` applies to exactly `Resource`. Names the grant doesn't hold are ignored, so revoking twice is harmless.
  Grants on ancestor URIs aren't touched, so the principal may still pass a check afterwards; `WhoHasAccess` shows
  where access comes from.
- Both are sent once and never retried automatically (see [Retries and rate limits](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/go/#retries-and-rate-limits)).
- `client.GetGrant(ctx, principal, resource)` returns the `*Grant` made on exactly that URI, not inherited ones. The
  API returns role IDs only, so `RoleRef.Name` is empty there.

#### Permissions and roles

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `CreatePermission(ctx, name, description)` | `*Permission`. Creating one that already exists with the same description succeeds; with another description it fails with `KindAlreadyExists`. |
| `GetPermission(ctx, name)` | `*Permission`, or an error of kind `KindNotFound`. |
| `UpdatePermission(ctx, name, newName, description)` | `*Permission`. Replaces the description and, when `newName` isn't empty, renames it. |
| `DeletePermission(ctx, name)` | `error`. Also deletes every grant of it. Succeeds if it doesn't exist. |
| `CreateRole(ctx, name, description, permissions)` | `*Role`, with its `ID`. Fails with `KindAlreadyExists` if a role with this name has other permissions or another description. |
| `GetRole(ctx, id)` | `*Role`. |
| `UpdateRole(ctx, id, name, description, permissions)` | `*Role`. Replaces the name, description and permissions. |
| `DeleteRole(ctx, id)` | `error`. |

`Permission` has `Name` and `Description`. `Role` has `ID`, `Name`, `Description` and `Permissions` (names, sorted).

```go
role, err := client.CreateRole(ctx, "viewer", "Read documents", []string{"document.read"})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
err = client.Grant(ctx, permio.GrantRequest{Principal: "alice", Resource: "/documents", Roles: []string{role.ID}})
```

### Groups

A [group](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/) is a named set of principals in a project. Grant to the group's principal ID,
`group:<slug>`, and every member holds the grant. Checks include the principal's groups automatically.

`permio.GroupPrincipal(slug)` returns the group's principal ID. `client.Groups()` returns the group operations, in
the client's project:

```go
groups := client.Groups()

if _, err := groups.Create(ctx, "editors", "Can edit every document"); err != nil {
    return err
}
if _, err := groups.AddMembers(ctx, "editors", []string{"alice", "bob"}); err != nil {
    return err
}
err := client.Grant(ctx, permio.GrantRequest{
    Principal:   permio.GroupPrincipal("editors"), // "group:editors"
    Resource:    "/documents",
    Permissions: []string{"document.write"},
})

ok, err := client.Check(ctx, "alice", "document.write", "/documents/42") // true
```

Every method that takes a group accepts its slug (`"editors"`) or its principal ID (`"group:editors"`). The slug
must be 1–64 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, or the call fails with `KindValidation` before anything is
sent (`permio.ValidateGroupName` runs the same check).

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `Create(ctx, name, description)` | `*Group`. Fails with `KindAlreadyExists` if the project already has a group with this name. |
| `Get(ctx, name)` | `*Group`, or an error of kind `KindNotFound`. |
| `Update(ctx, name, description)` | `*Group`. Replaces the description; a group can't be renamed. |
| `Delete(ctx, name)` | `error`. Deletes the group, its memberships and every grant made to it. Succeeds whether or not it existed. |
| `List(ctx, opts)` | `iter.Seq2[Group, error]`, ordered by name. `opts.Search` filters by name. |
| `AddMembers(ctx, name, principals)` | `*MembershipChange`: `Changed` (added) and `Unchanged` (already members), in request order. |
| `RemoveMembers(ctx, name, principals)` | `*MembershipChange`: `Changed` (removed) and `Unchanged` (weren't members), in request order. |
| `ListMembers(ctx, name, opts)` | `iter.Seq2[GroupMember, error]` (`PrincipalID`, `CreatedAt`), ordered by principal ID. |
| `ListForPrincipal(ctx, principal, opts)` | `iter.Seq2[Group, error]`: the groups the principal is a member of, ordered by name. |

- `AddMembers` and `RemoveMembers` remove duplicates and send 100 principals per call. If a later call fails, the
  result holds the changes made by the calls that succeeded, alongside the error.
- `AddMembers` rejects `group:` IDs with `KindValidation`, because groups can't contain groups.
- `Group` has `Name`, `Description`, `PrincipalID` (`"group:<name>"`), `CreatedAt` and `UpdatedAt`.

```go
change, err := groups.AddMembers(ctx, "group:editors", []string{"alice", "carol"})
// change.Changed: [carol], change.Unchanged: [alice]

for m, err := range groups.ListMembers(ctx, "editors", nil) {
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    fmt.Println(m.PrincipalID)
}
```

Reading groups works with a check-access API key. Creating, updating and deleting groups and changing members needs
a key with full access, and changing members also needs the right to grant across the project. See
[Permissions you need](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/#permissions-you-need).

### Resource URIs

Resource URIs are paths such as `/projects/p1/documents/42`. A grant on a URI also covers every URI beneath it. See
[Resources and inheritance](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/resources/) for the full rules.

#### `Resource(segments...)`

Builds a URI from raw segments. It adds the leading `/` and percent-encodes each segment, so an ID that contains
`/`, spaces or other reserved characters stays a single segment:

```go
permio.Resource("projects", "p1", "documents", "42") // "/projects/p1/documents/42"
permio.Resource("files", "reports/2026.pdf")         // "/files/reports%2F2026.pdf"
```

Only `A–Z`, `a–z`, `0–9` and `- _ . ~` are left as they are. Segments are strings, so convert numeric IDs yourself
(`strconv.Itoa`). An empty segment produces a URI that every call rejects.

**Tip**

Build URIs the same way when you grant and when you check, or they will not match.

#### Other helpers

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `EncodeSegment(segment)` | Encodes one segment the way `Resource` does. |
| `ValidateResourceURI(uri)` | Returns an error of kind `KindValidation` unless `uri` has the basic shape the API accepts: a leading `/`, no empty segments, no whitespace or control characters, no regular-expression metacharacters (below) and at most 2048 bytes. |
| `MaxResourceURILength` | `2048`. |
| `GroupPrincipal(slug)` | `"group:" + slug`. |
| `GroupPrefix` | `"group:"`. |
| `ValidateGroupName(slug)` | Returns an error of kind `KindValidation` unless the slug is 1–64 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. |
| `WildcardSegment` | `"_"`, which in a stored grant URI or a pattern scope matches exactly one segment. |

The metacharacters `ValidateResourceURI` rejects are `( ) [ ] { } * + ? | ^ $ \`. Every helper that takes a resource
URI runs it before sending; the API enforces the remaining rules and answers with `InvalidArgument`
(`KindValidation`).

### Errors

Every call that fails returns a `*permio.Error`, including calls made through the
[raw clients](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/go/#raw-clients-full-api). It has these fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Kind` | A `permio.Kind` that classifies the error (below). |
| `Code` | The gRPC `codes.Code`. `codes.OK` for errors the SDK raises itself (`KindConfig`, `KindDenied`), `codes.InvalidArgument` for its own input checks. |
| `Message` | The server's or the SDK's message. |
| `Missing` | For `KindPermission`, what the API key lacks; for `KindDenied`, what the principal lacks. |
| `Principal` | The checked principal, for `KindDenied`. |
| `RetryAfter` | The delay the server asked for, for `KindRateLimited` and sometimes `KindUnavailable`. Zero when it gave none. |
| `Metadata` | The response headers and trailers. |

Match a kind with `errors.Is` and the `Err…` sentinel, and read the fields with `errors.As`:

| Kind | Sentinel | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KindConfig` | `ErrConfig` | Bad client setup: a malformed API key, an invalid endpoint or no project. |
| `KindAuth` | `ErrAuth` | `Unauthenticated`: the key is missing, unknown or invalidated. |
| `KindPermission` | `ErrPermission` | `PermissionDenied`: the **API key** lacks the rights for this call. |
| `KindValidation` | `ErrValidation` | `InvalidArgument`, or the SDK's own input checks. |
| `KindNotFound` | `ErrNotFound` | `NotFound`, for example `GetPermission` for a name that doesn't exist. |
| `KindAlreadyExists` | `ErrAlreadyExists` | `AlreadyExists`. |
| `KindUnavailable` | `ErrUnavailable` | `Unavailable`, including network failures. |
| `KindTimeout` | `ErrTimeout` | `DeadlineExceeded`, from `Options.Timeout` or the context's deadline. |
| `KindRateLimited` | `ErrRateLimited` | `ResourceExhausted`: the organisation's rate limit is used up. |
| `KindDenied` | `ErrDenied` | Returned only by `Assert` and `AssertAll`, when the **principal** is not allowed. |
| `KindOther` | none | Anything else, including cancellation of the context. |

`permio.KindOf(err)` returns the kind (or `""` for other errors), and `permio.IsNotFound(err)` is a shortcut.
`*Error` also implements `GRPCStatus()`, so `status.Code(err)` works, and `Unwrap()` returns the underlying gRPC or
context error.

**Note: Denied is not an error**

`KindPermission` is about the *caller*. It means your API key is not allowed to make the call: for `Check`, the
key needs `permission.check` on the checked resources and on the principal. A principal failing a check is a
normal result: `Check` returns `false` with a `nil` error, and only `Assert` returns an error, of kind
`KindDenied`.

For `KindPermission`, `Missing` uses the API's fully qualified URIs (`/organisation/{org}/project/{project}/...`),
not the URIs you sent.

```go
err := client.Assert(ctx, "alice", "document.write", "/documents/1")

var perr *permio.Error
switch {
case err == nil:
    // allowed
case errors.Is(err, permio.ErrDenied):
    // the principal may not do this: respond with 403
case errors.Is(err, permio.ErrPermission):
    // the API key may not run this check (it needs permission.check)
    errors.As(err, &perr)
    log.Println(perr.Missing)
case errors.Is(err, permio.ErrAuth):
    // the API key is missing, unknown or invalidated
case errors.As(err, &perr):
    log.Println(perr.Kind, perr.Code, perr.Message)
}
```

`permio.ParseMissingPermissions(message)` extracts the missing list from a `PermissionDenied` message. You only need
it if you call the API without the SDK's connection.

### Retries and rate limits

- **Retried:** idempotent reads (`Check`, `BatchCheck`, `WhoAmI`, and every `Get*` and `List*` RPC, including
  `ListAccess`, `ListPrincipalsWithAccess` and the group reads) are retried on `Unavailable` and
  `DeadlineExceeded`. They are retried twice by default, with exponential backoff and jitter.
- **Never retried:** writes (every Create, Update, Delete, Grant, Revoke, adding and removing group members, and so
  on) are sent exactly once. Grant and revoke converge on the server, so you can repeat them yourself after a
  timeout, as long as nobody else is changing that grant in the meantime.
- **Rate limits:** a rate-limited read (`ResourceExhausted`) is retried after the delay the server asks for (a
  `google.rpc.RetryInfo` detail, else a `retry-after` header), when that delay is within `RetryOptions.MaxDelay`.
  Otherwise, and for writes, the call fails with `KindRateLimited` and `RetryAfter` set. `ResourceExhausted` without
  a delay is not retried. A `retry-after` on `Unavailable` is used as the minimum backoff.
- **Timeouts:** `Options.Timeout` applies to each attempt (default 10 s). The context's deadline is an overall
  deadline across all attempts, and cancelling the context stops any pending retry.

```go
client, err := permio.New(permio.Options{
    APIKey:  os.Getenv("PERMIO_API_KEY"),
    Project: "default",
    Timeout: 5 * time.Second,
    Retry: permio.RetryOptions{
        MaxRetries: 3,
        BaseDelay:  100 * time.Millisecond,
        MaxDelay:   2 * time.Second,
    },
})

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 8*time.Second) // overall deadline for this call
defer cancel()
ok, err := client.Check(ctx, "alice", "document.read", "/documents/1")
```

`RetryOptions` has these fields:

- `MaxRetries`: retries after the first attempt. Zero means the default, 2; a negative value disables retries.
- `BaseDelay`: the first delay, which doubles each time. Default 100 ms.
- `MaxDelay`: the cap on a single delay, and the longest server-requested delay the SDK will wait for. Default 2 s.

If you handle rate limiting yourself, wait for `RetryAfter`:

```go
var perr *permio.Error
if errors.As(err, &perr) && perr.Kind == permio.KindRateLimited {
    time.Sleep(perr.RetryAfter)
}
```

`permio.IsIdempotent("/permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService/Check")` tells you whether the SDK retries a given
RPC.

### Listing with iterators

List RPCs are paginated with a cursor (see [Pagination](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/pagination/)). The list helpers return
`iter.Seq2[T, error]` iterators that fetch pages as you go. Breaking out of the loop stops fetching:

```go
for p, err := range client.ListPermissions(ctx, &permio.ListOptions{Search: "document."}) {
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    fmt.Println(p.Name)
}

roles, err := permio.Collect(client.ListRoles(ctx, nil))
```

A failing page yields the error once and ends the iteration. `permio.Collect` gathers a listing into a slice and
stops at the first error.

| Method | Yields |
| --- | --- |
| `ListPermissions(ctx, opts)` | `Permission` |
| `ListRoles(ctx, opts)` | `Role` (with its `Permissions`) |
| `ListPrincipals(ctx, opts)` | `string` principal IDs that have grants in the project, groups included as `group:<slug>` |
| `ListAssignments(ctx, principal, opts)` | `Grant` (`Principal`, `Resource`, `Roles`, `Permissions`), one per resource URI |
| `Groups().List(ctx, opts)` | `Group` |
| `Groups().ListMembers(ctx, name, opts)` | `GroupMember` |
| `Groups().ListForPrincipal(ctx, principal, opts)` | `Group` |

`opts` is a `*permio.ListOptions` and may be `nil`:

- `PageSize`: 1–100, default 100 (`permio.MaxPageSize`).
- `Search`: filters by name. `ListPermissions`, `ListRoles`, `ListPrincipals` and `Groups().List` use it; the others
  ignore it.

There is no public helper for other list RPCs. Follow `next_cursor` yourself through the raw clients, as in the
example below.

### Raw clients (full API)

`client.Permissions()` and `client.Organisations()` return the generated gRPC clients for
`permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService` and `permio.organisation.v1.OrganisationService`. Authentication,
timeouts, retries and error mapping are already applied. Every RPC in the [API reference](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/)
is available, with request and response types generated from the protobuf definitions. Method names are the RPC
names, and fields are in Go's CamelCase. Set `ProjectName` on requests yourself; the client's default project isn't
applied:

```go
import (
    permissionsv1 "github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go/proto/permissions/v1"
)

perm, err := client.Permissions().CreatePermission(ctx, &permissionsv1.CreatePermissionRequest{
    ProjectName: "default",
    Name:        "document.read",
    Description: "Read documents",
})

res, err := client.Permissions().Check(ctx, &permissionsv1.CheckPermissionRequest{
    ProjectName:  "default",
    PrincipalId:  "alice",
    ResourceUris: []string{"/documents/42"},
    Permissions:  []string{"document.read"},
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Println(res.GetPassed(), res.GetMissingPermissions())
```

A list RPC without a helper, following the cursor by hand:

```go
import (
    organisationv1 "github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go/proto/organisation/v1"
    paginationv1 "github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go/proto/pagination/v1"
    "google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"
)

var cursor *string
for {
    page, err := client.Organisations().ListAPIKeys(ctx, &organisationv1.ListAPIKeysRequest{
        OrganisationId: "your-org-id",
        ProjectName:    "default",
        Pagination:     &paginationv1.PaginationRequest{Limit: proto.Int32(100), Cursor: cursor},
    })
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    for _, k := range page.GetApiKeys() {
        fmt.Println(k.GetName())
    }
    next := page.GetPagination().GetNextCursor()
    if next == "" {
        break
    }
    cursor = proto.String(next)
}
```

`client.Conn()` returns the wrapped `grpc.ClientConnInterface`, for any other generated client.

| Import path | Package | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go/proto/permissions/v1` | `permissionsv1` | `PermissionsService` client; permission, role, check, access and group messages |
| `github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go/proto/organisation/v1` | `organisationv1` | `OrganisationService` client; organisation, project and API key messages |
| `github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go/proto/pagination/v1` | `paginationv1` | Pagination request and response messages |

**Note: What a key can call**

By default an API key has **check** access: it can run checks and access queries, and read permissions, roles,
principals, assignments and groups. Creating, updating or deleting permissions, roles and groups, granting or
revoking, and changing group members needs a key with full access. See
[API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels).

### API key helpers

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ValidateAPIKey(key)` | Returns `APIKeyOpaque` for `perms_` keys and `APIKeyJWT` for legacy JWT keys, or an error of kind `KindConfig` if the key is malformed. |
| `APIKeyLength` | `44`, the length of a `perms_` key. |
| `EnvAPIKey` | `"PERMIO_API_KEY"`. |

These only check the shape and checksum. Only the API can tell you whether a key exists and is still valid: use
[`WhoAmI`](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/go/#verifying-the-key).

### net/http

```go
func requirePermission(client *permio.Client, permission string, next http.Handler) http.Handler {
    return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        userID := userIDFrom(r.Context()) // set by your auth middleware
        err := client.Assert(r.Context(), userID, permission, permio.Resource("documents", r.PathValue("id")))
        switch {
        case err == nil:
            next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
        case errors.Is(err, permio.ErrDenied):
            http.Error(w, "forbidden", http.StatusForbidden)
        default:
            // any other error: auth, validation, network...
            http.Error(w, "authorisation unavailable", http.StatusServiceUnavailable)
        }
    })
}

mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle("GET /documents/{id}", requirePermission(client, "document.read", http.HandlerFunc(getDocument)))
```

### How it talks to the API

The SDK uses native gRPC over HTTP/2 with TLS, through `google.golang.org/grpc`. The key is sent as
`authorization: Bearer <key>` metadata on every call. Timeouts are applied as context deadlines on each attempt.

---

Source: https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/

## Python SDK

`permio` is the official Python client for the perms.io API. It wraps the API in a few calls for asking "may this
principal do X on this resource?", granting and revoking, managing groups and answering "where?" and "who?"
questions. It also gives you typed errors, retries for idempotent reads and iterators over list endpoints. The full
generated API is there too, as an escape hatch.

- Runs on Python 3.9 and later. It is fully typed (`py.typed`).
- Comes with two clients that have the same methods: `Permio` (synchronous) and `AsyncPermio` (asyncio).
- Talks native gRPC over TLS through `grpcio` (`grpc.aio` for `AsyncPermio`).
- Has three runtime dependencies: `grpcio`, `protobuf` and `googleapis-common-protos`.

**Note: Versions**

This page describes **0.1.0**, the first release on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/permio/).

### Install

```bash
pip install permio
```

### Quick start

**Sync**

```python
from permio import Permio, resource

permio = Permio(project="default")  # API key from $PERMIO_API_KEY

if permio.check("alice", "document.read", resource("documents", 42)):  # "/documents/42"
    print("alice may read document 42")
```

**Async**

```python
from permio import AsyncPermio, resource

async with AsyncPermio(project="default") as permio:  # API key from $PERMIO_API_KEY
    if await permio.check("alice", "document.read", resource("documents", 42)):
        print("alice may read document 42")
```

The arguments are always `principal, permission, resource`, in that order. A principal that lacks the permission is
a normal answer: `check` returns `False`.

### Configuration

```python
from permio import DEV_BASE_URL, Permio, RetryOptions

permio = Permio(
    api_key="perms_...",    # default: $PERMIO_API_KEY
    base_url=DEV_BASE_URL,  # default: https://api.perms.io
    project="default",      # default project for every call
    timeout=10,             # seconds per attempt
    retries=RetryOptions(max_retries=2, base_delay=0.1, max_delay=2.0),
)
```

The constructor checks the API key's format and checksum straight away. A missing, mistyped or truncated key raises
`PermioConfigError` before any request is sent. See [API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/) for the format.

#### Options

`api_key` is the only positional argument; the rest are keyword-only. `AsyncPermio` takes the same options.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api_key` | `str` | `$PERMIO_API_KEY` | A `perms_…` key from the dashboard, or a legacy JWT key. |
| `base_url` | `str` | `https://api.perms.io` | API host: `https://host[:port]` (TLS), `http://host:port` (plaintext, for a local server) or `host:port` (TLS). It can't have a path. |
| `project` | `str` | none | Default project for every call. Each call can override it with `project=`. A call with neither raises `PermioConfigError`. |
| `timeout` | `float` | `10` | Timeout for each attempt, in seconds. `0` disables it. |
| `retries` | `int \| RetryOptions` | `2` | Retries for idempotent reads. An `int` sets `max_retries`; see [Retries and rate limits](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#retries-and-rate-limits). |
| `channel` | `grpc.Channel` | none | Your own channel (`grpc.aio.Channel` for `AsyncPermio`), for example for a proxy or custom credentials. `base_url` and `channel_options` are then ignored, and the client doesn't close it. |
| `channel_options` | `list[tuple[str, Any]]` | none | Extra gRPC channel options, used when the client creates the channel. |

#### Production and development

| Constant | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | `https://api.perms.io` (production, the default) |
| `DEV_BASE_URL` | `https://dev-api.perms.io` (development) |

Keys belong to one environment, so a production key won't work against the development API. `who_am_i()` tells you
which organisation and project a key belongs to and whether it can write. It is the one call that needs no project,
which makes it useful for checking a key at startup:

```python
me = permio.who_am_i()
print(me.kind, me.project, me.api_key_access)  # "api_key" "default" "check" (or "full")
```

`WhoAmI` has `principal_id`, `organisation_id`, `kind` (`"user"`, `"api_key"`, `"service_account"` or `"unknown"`),
`project`, `api_key_access` (`"check"`, `"full"` or `"unknown"`; `None` for credentials other than API keys) and
`email`.

The client also exposes `permio.project`, `permio.base_url`, `permio.api_key_kind` (`"opaque"` or `"jwt"`) and
`permio.channel`.

#### Per-call options

Every method also takes these keyword arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | Project for this call. Defaults to the client's `project`. (`who_am_i` doesn't take it.) |
| `timeout` | Overall deadline for this call in seconds, across retries. |
| `metadata` | Extra request headers, as `[("name", "value"), ...]`. An `authorization` entry is ignored; the client always sends its own key. |

#### Closing the client

Create one client per process and share it. `close()` closes the gRPC channel if the client created it. Both
clients are context managers:

**Sync**

```python
with Permio(project="default") as permio:
    ...

# or
permio = Permio(project="default")
...
permio.close()
```

**Async**

```python
async with AsyncPermio(project="default") as permio:
    ...

# or
permio = AsyncPermio(project="default")
...
await permio.close()
```

**Note: Async**

On `AsyncPermio`, every method on this page is a coroutine and must be awaited, except the list helpers, which
return async iterators for `async for`. The examples below use the sync client.

### Checking permissions

The check helpers all take the same arguments:

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `principal` | Required. The ID of the user, service or other principal being checked. |
| `permission` | Required. One permission name, or a list of up to 100. |
| `resource` | Required. One resource URI, or a list of up to 100. Every resource is checked. |
| `project`, `timeout`, `metadata` | As in [Per-call options](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#per-call-options). |

Duplicates are removed before sending. Each URI is checked with `assert_resource_uri()` first, so a malformed one
raises `PermioValidationError` without a request.

#### `check`

Returns `True` when the principal holds **every** permission on **every** resource:

```python
permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42")                        # -> bool
permio.check("alice", ["document.read", "document.write"], "/documents/42")    # both
permio.check("alice", "document.read", ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"])       # on both
```

It only raises when the call itself fails, for example because of a bad key, malformed input or network trouble.

#### `check_detailed`

Same question, but it also tells you what is missing, per resource:

```python
result = permio.check_detailed("alice", "document.read", ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"])
result.allowed  # False
result.missing  # [MissingPermission(resource="/invoices/1", permissions=["document.read"])]
```

It returns a `CheckResult` with `allowed` and `missing`, a list of `MissingPermission` (`resource`, `permissions`).
`missing` is empty when `allowed` is `True`. A `CheckResult` is truthy when `allowed` is `True`.

#### `assert_allowed`

Returns `None` when the principal is allowed and raises `PermioDeniedError` when it is not. (`assert` is a Python
keyword, hence the name.) The error carries `principal` and `missing`:

```python
permio.assert_allowed("alice", "document.write", "/documents/42")
```

#### `check_any`

Returns `True` when, **on every resource**, the principal holds **at least one** of the permissions. It is still a
single API call:

```python
permio.check_any("alice", ["document.admin", "document.write"], "/documents/42")
```

#### `check_all`

An alias of `check`: every permission on every resource.

#### Batch checks

`check` gives one answer for all its resources together. `batch_check` answers **each resource separately**, which is
what you need to filter a list or decide which rows get an "edit" button. It returns a `dict` from resource URI to
allowed, with one entry per distinct resource, in request order:

```python
from permio import resource

allowed = permio.batch_check("alice", "document.read", [resource("documents", d.id) for d in docs])
visible = [d for d in docs if allowed[resource("documents", d.id)]]
```

`batch_check_detailed` asks the same question but returns a list of `BatchCheckEntry` (`resource`, `allowed`,
`missing`) in request order. Here `missing` is a list of permission names:

```python
for entry in permio.batch_check_detailed(
    "alice", ["document.read", "document.write"], ["/documents/1", "/documents/2"]
):
    print(entry.resource, entry.allowed, entry.missing)
# /documents/1 True []
# /documents/2 False ['document.write']
```

- `resources` must be a list (or other iterable) of URIs, not a single string. Duplicates are sent once.
- A resource is allowed only with **all** the permissions (up to 100).
- More than 100 resources are split into several `BatchCheck` calls. `Permio` sends them one after another;
  `AsyncPermio` sends them in parallel.
- The SDK fails closed: if the API's answer lacks a result for any requested resource, it raises a `PermioError`
  instead of guessing.

#### Access queries

These answer "where?" and "who?" rather than "may they?". The
[Filtering lists and building share dialogs](https://docs.perms.io/guides/filtering-and-sharing/) guide shows them in context.

##### `list_access`

`list_access(principal, permission, under)` answers "where may this principal use this permission, at or below
`under`?". It follows every page and returns an `AccessScopes` object:

```python
access = permio.list_access("alice", "document.read", "/documents")

if access.covers_all:
    ...  # alice may read everything under /documents: no filter needed
else:
    print(access.to_prefixes())  # e.g. ["/documents/4", "/documents/7"]
```

Access through roles and groups counts. `permission` is a single name, and a `_` segment in `under` is literal. It
also takes `page_size`, and its `timeout` and `metadata` apply to each page. The API key needs `permission.check` on
`under` and `principal.assignment.get` on the principal.

`AccessScopes`:

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `under` | `str` | The URI that was asked about. |
| `covers_all` | `bool` | The principal holds the permission on `under` itself, so on everything below it. Check this first. |
| `scopes` | `tuple[AccessScopeInfo, ...]` | `AccessScopeInfo(uri, kind)`, ordered by URI. `kind` is `"subtree"`, `"pattern"`, `"exact"` (reserved, not returned today) or `"unknown"` (a kind this SDK version doesn't know; it never matches). |
| `is_empty` | `bool` | No access anywhere under `under`. |
| `allows(uri)` | `bool` | Whether `uri` is covered. Matches per segment: `/a/b` covers `/a/b/c` but not `/a/bc`. Malformed URIs are never allowed. |
| `to_prefixes()` | `list[str]` | The subtree URIs, for prefix filters. Prefixes covered by a shorter one are dropped. Pattern scopes aren't included. |
| `patterns()` | `list[str]` | The pattern URIs, with `_` segments. |
| `has_patterns` | `bool` | Some scope is a pattern, so `to_prefixes()` alone doesn't cover everything. |
| `exact()` | `list[str]` | The exact URIs. Empty today. |
| `to_regex()` | `re.Pattern[str]` | One anchored regular expression matching exactly what `allows()` accepts. Use `.pattern` for MongoDB `$regex` or PostgreSQL `~`. Matches nothing when there are no scopes. |

**Warning**

A prefix `p` from `to_prefixes()` means `p` **and everything below it**. Filter with
`path = p OR path starts with p + "/"`, never a bare "starts with `p`", which would let `/documents/1` match
`/documents/12`. In SQL, use `starts_with(path, p || '/')` rather than `LIKE`, where `_` is a wildcard.

For a URI outside `under`, `allows()` returning `False` means "not asked", not "denied".

##### `who_has_access`

`who_has_access(resource, *, permission=None, expand_groups=False)` answers "who has access to this resource?". It
follows every page and returns a list of `AccessEntry`, ordered by principal ID:

```python
for entry in permio.who_has_access("/documents/42", permission="document.read", expand_groups=True):
    print(entry.principal, entry.is_group, entry.via_group,
          [(g.resource, g.match, g.source.type) for g in entry.via])
# alice False None [('/documents', 'ancestor', 'role')]
# bob False editors [('/documents', 'ancestor', 'direct')]
# group:editors True None [('/documents', 'ancestor', 'direct')]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `resource` | Required. The resource to look at. A `_` segment here is literal. |
| `permission` | Optional. Only count grants that confer this permission, so a principal is listed exactly when `check()` passes for it through its own grants (or, for entries with `via_group`, through that group). Unset, any grant counts. |
| `expand_groups` | Optional. Also list every member of each listed group, once per group, with `via_group` set. |
| `project`, `page_size`, `timeout`, `metadata` | As for `list_access`. |

`AccessEntry` has `principal`, `is_group`, `via_group` (a group slug, or `None`) and `via`, the grants that give the
access, most specific first. Each grant (`AccessGrantInfo`) has:

- `resource`: the URI the grant was made on (the resource, an ancestor, or a `_` wildcard URI that matches it);
- `inherited`: `True` unless the grant was made on exactly the resource;
- `match`: `"exact"`, `"ancestor"`, `"wildcard"` or `"unknown"`;
- `source`: an `AccessGrantSource` whose `type` is `"role"` (with the role's `id` and `name`), `"direct"` for
  directly granted permissions, or `"unknown"`.

The API key needs `principal.list` and `principal.assignment.list` on the project.

### Granting and revoking

`grant` and `revoke` need an API key with full access. Both take a principal and one resource URI, then
`permissions` (permission names) and `roles` (role IDs) as keyword arguments. Each takes one value or a list, and at
least one permission or role is required.

```python
permio.grant("alice", "/documents/42", permissions="document.read")
permio.grant("alice", "/documents", permissions=["document.read", "document.write"], roles="ROLE_ID")

permio.revoke("alice", "/documents/42", permissions="document.read")
```

- A grant applies to the URI and everything beneath it. Grants are additive: what the principal already holds there
  is kept. A permission or role that doesn't exist in the project raises `PermioValidationError`.
- `revoke` removes names from the grant on **exactly** that URI. Grants on ancestor URIs stay, so `check()` may still
  pass afterwards; `who_has_access()` shows where access comes from. Names the grant doesn't hold are ignored, so
  revoking twice is harmless.
- Roles are referenced by ID. Find them with `list_roles()`.
- Neither call is ever retried automatically. After a timeout, the first attempt may still have landed.
- Both return `None`.

There are no helpers for creating permissions and roles; use the [raw client](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#raw-client-full-api).

### Groups

A [group](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/) is a named set of principals in a project. Grant to the group's principal ID,
`group:<slug>`, and every member holds the grant. Checks include the principal's groups automatically.

#### `group(slug)`

Returns the group's principal ID. It raises `PermioValidationError` unless the slug is 1–64 lower-case letters,
digits and hyphens.

```python
from permio import group

group("editors")  # "group:editors"

permio.groups.create("editors", description="Can edit every document")
permio.groups.add_members("editors", ["alice", "bob"])
permio.grant(group("editors"), "/documents", permissions="document.write")

permio.check("alice", "document.write", "/documents/42")  # True, through the group
```

#### `permio.groups`

Every method that takes a group accepts its slug (`"editors"`) or its principal ID (`"group:editors"`).

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `create(name, *, description="")` | `Group`. Raises a `PermioError` with code `grpc.StatusCode.ALREADY_EXISTS` if the project already has a group with this name. |
| `get(name)` | `Group`. Raises `PermioNotFoundError` if it doesn't exist. |
| `update(name, *, description)` | `Group`. Replaces the description; a group can't be renamed. |
| `delete(name)` | `None`. Deletes the group, its memberships and every grant made to it, whether or not it existed. |
| `list(*, search=None)` | Iterator of `Group`, ordered by name. |
| `add_members(name, principals)` | `AddMembersResult(added, existing)`, each a list in request order. |
| `remove_members(name, principals)` | `RemoveMembersResult(removed, not_members)`, each a list in request order. |
| `list_members(name)` | Iterator of `GroupMember` (`principal_id`, `created_at`), ordered by principal ID. |
| `list_for_principal(principal)` | Iterator of the `Group`s the principal is a member of, ordered by name. |

- `add_members` and `remove_members` take a list of 1–100 principals; duplicates are removed. `add_members` rejects
  `group:` IDs with `PermioValidationError`, because groups can't contain groups.
- Every method also takes `project`, `timeout` and `metadata`. The list methods take `page_size` too, and their
  `timeout` and `metadata` apply to each page.
- `Group` and `GroupMember` are the generated protobuf messages. `Group` has `id`, `organisation_id`,
  `project_name`, `name`, `description`, `principal_id` (`"group:<name>"`), `created_at` and `updated_at`.
- On `AsyncPermio`, `permio.groups` is an `AsyncGroups` with the same methods.

```python
res = permio.groups.add_members("group:editors", ["alice", "carol"])
print(res.added, res.existing)

for m in permio.groups.list_members("editors"):
    print(m.principal_id)
for g in permio.groups.list_for_principal("alice"):
    print(g.name)
```

Reading groups works with a check-access API key. Creating, updating and deleting groups and changing members needs
a key with full access, and changing members also needs the right to grant across the project. See
[Permissions you need](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/#permissions-you-need).

### Resource URIs

Resource URIs are paths such as `/projects/p1/documents/42`. A grant on a URI also covers every URI beneath it. See
[Resources and inheritance](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/resources/) for the full rules.

#### `resource(*segments)`

Builds a URI from raw segments (strings or integers). It adds the leading `/` and percent-encodes each segment, so an
ID that contains `/`, spaces or other reserved characters stays a single segment:

```python
from permio import resource

resource("projects", "p1", "documents", 42)  # "/projects/p1/documents/42"
resource("files", "reports/2026.pdf")        # "/files/reports%2F2026.pdf"
```

Everything except `A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~` is encoded as UTF-8, including `( ) *`, which the API rejects in segments.
The output matches the TypeScript SDK's `resource()`. Empty segments, or no segments, raise `PermioValidationError`.

**Tip**

Build URIs the same way when you grant and when you check, or they will not match.

#### Other helpers

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `encode_segment(segment)` | Encodes one segment the way `resource()` does. |
| `assert_resource_uri(uri)` | Raises `PermioValidationError` unless `uri` has the basic shape the API accepts: a leading `/`, no empty segments, no whitespace or control characters, and at most 2048 bytes. |
| `MAX_RESOURCE_URI_LENGTH` | `2048`. |
| `WILDCARD_SEGMENT` | `"_"`. |
| `GROUP_PRINCIPAL_PREFIX` | `"group:"`. |

Every helper runs `assert_resource_uri` on its URIs before sending. The API enforces the remaining rules, such as no
`( ) [ ] { } * + ? | ^ $ \` in segments, and answers with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, which the SDK raises as
`PermioValidationError`.

### Errors

Every error the SDK raises extends `PermioError`. It has these attributes:

- `code`: the `grpc.StatusCode`, or `None` for errors the SDK raises itself (bad configuration, failed input checks,
  `PermioDeniedError`).
- `code_name`: the code's name in lower case, for example `"permission_denied"`, or `None`.
- `message`: the error message.
- `metadata`: the response headers and trailers, as a tuple of `(name, value)` pairs.

The original `grpc.RpcError` is chained as `__cause__`.

| Class | When |
| --- | --- |
| `PermioConfigError` | Bad client setup: a missing or malformed API key, no `project`, an invalid `base_url`, `timeout` or `retries`. |
| `PermioAuthError` | `UNAUTHENTICATED`: the key is missing, unknown or invalidated. |
| `PermioPermissionError` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`: the **API key** lacks the rights for this call. `missing` lists what it lacks when the API says. |
| `PermioValidationError` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, or the SDK's own input checks (for example a URI without a leading `/`). |
| `PermioNotFoundError` | `NOT_FOUND`, for example `groups.get()` for a group that doesn't exist. |
| `PermioUnavailableError` | `UNAVAILABLE`, including network failures. |
| `PermioTimeoutError` | `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, including the SDK's own deadlines. |
| `PermioRateLimitError` | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`: the organisation's rate limit is used up. `retry_after` is the delay the server asked for, in seconds, or `None`. |
| `PermioDeniedError` | Raised only by `assert_allowed()`, when the **principal** is not allowed. Has `principal` and `missing`. |

Any other status, such as `ALREADY_EXISTS`, is a plain `PermioError` with the matching `code`.

**Note: Denied is not an error**

`PermioPermissionError` is about the *caller*. It means your API key is not allowed to make the call: for
`Check`, the key needs `permission.check` on the checked resources and on the principal. A principal failing a
check is a normal result: `check()` returns `False` and `assert_allowed()` raises `PermioDeniedError`.

`PermioPermissionError.missing` uses the API's fully qualified URIs (`/organisation/{org}/project/{project}/...`),
not the URIs you sent.

```python
from permio import PermioAuthError, PermioDeniedError, PermioError, PermioPermissionError, resource

try:
    permio.assert_allowed(user_id, "document.write", resource("documents", doc_id))
except PermioDeniedError:
    ...  # the principal may not do this: respond with 403
except PermioPermissionError as err:
    print(err.missing)  # the API key may not run this check (it needs permission.check)
except PermioAuthError:
    ...  # the API key is missing, unknown or invalidated
except PermioError as err:
    print(err.code_name, err.message)
```

`parse_missing_permissions(message)` extracts the missing list from a `PERMISSION_DENIED` message. You only need it
if you call the generated stubs without the SDK.

### Retries and rate limits

- **Retries:** idempotent reads (`Check`, `BatchCheck`, `WhoAmI`, and every `Get*` and `List*` RPC, including
  `ListAccess`, `ListPrincipalsWithAccess` and the group reads) are retried on `UNAVAILABLE` and
  `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. They are retried twice by default, with exponential backoff and jitter. Network failures
  count as `UNAVAILABLE`.
- **Writes** (every Create, Update, Delete, Grant, Revoke, Invite, adding and removing group members, and so on)
  are never retried.
- **Timeouts:**
    - The client's `timeout` applies to each attempt (default 10 seconds).
    - A call's `timeout=` is an overall deadline across all attempts. If a retry couldn't finish its backoff
      before the deadline, the last error is raised instead.
    - On `AsyncPermio`, cancelling the task cancels the call and any pending retry.

```python
permio = Permio(
    project="default",
    timeout=5,
    retries=RetryOptions(max_retries=3, base_delay=0.1, max_delay=2.0),
)

permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/1", timeout=8)
```

`RetryOptions` is a frozen dataclass with these fields:

- `max_retries`: retries after the first attempt. Default 2. `retries=0` turns retries off.
- `base_delay`: the first delay in seconds, which doubles each time. Default 0.1.
- `max_delay`: the cap on a single delay in seconds. Default 2.0.

Each delay is picked at random between half and all of `min(max_delay, base_delay * 2**attempt)`.

#### Rate limits

When the API answers `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, the SDK looks for the delay the server asked for: a
`google.rpc.RetryInfo` detail, or else a `retry-after` header (seconds or an HTTP date).

- An idempotent read is retried after that delay, plus a little jitter, if the delay is no longer than `max_delay`
  and a retry is left.
- Otherwise, including when the server gave no delay and for every write, the call raises `PermioRateLimitError` with
  `retry_after` set. Waiting and trying again is then up to you.
- A `retry-after` header on `UNAVAILABLE` is honoured as the minimum backoff.

```python
import time

from permio import PermioRateLimitError

try:
    permio.grant("alice", "/documents/42", permissions="document.read")
except PermioRateLimitError as err:
    time.sleep(err.retry_after or 1)
    # ...try again, or queue the write
```

`is_idempotent_method("permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService.Check")` tells you whether the SDK retries a given
RPC.

### Listing with iterators

List RPCs are paginated with a cursor (see [Pagination](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/pagination/)). The list helpers return
iterators that fetch pages as you go. Each item is the generated protobuf message:

**Sync**

```python
for p in permio.list_permissions(search="document."):
    print(p.name)
for role in permio.list_roles():
    print(role.id, role.name, list(role.permissions))
for principal_id in permio.list_principals():
    print(principal_id)
for a in permio.list_assignments("alice"):
    print(a.resource_uri, list(a.roles))
```

**Async**

```python
async for p in permio.list_permissions(search="document."):
    print(p.name)
async for role in permio.list_roles():
    print(role.id, role.name, list(role.permissions))
async for principal_id in permio.list_principals():
    print(principal_id)
async for a in permio.list_assignments("alice"):
    print(a.resource_uri, list(a.roles))
```

| Method | Yields |
| --- | --- |
| `list_permissions(*, search=None)` | `Permission` |
| `list_roles(*, search=None)` | `Role` (with its `permissions`) |
| `list_principals(*, search=None)` | `str` principal IDs that have grants in the project |
| `list_assignments(principal)` | `Assignment` (`resource_uri`, `permissions`, `roles`) |
| `groups.list(*, search=None)` | `Group` (see [Groups](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#groups)) |
| `groups.list_members(name)` | `GroupMember` |
| `groups.list_for_principal(principal)` | `Group` |

Each method also takes these keyword arguments:

- `project`
- `page_size`: 1–100, default 100
- `timeout`: per page
- `metadata`

The project and principal are checked when you call the method; the first request is sent when you start iterating.
`list_access` and `who_has_access` follow every page themselves and return the complete result.

For any other list RPC, call the [raw client](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#raw-client-full-api) and follow `pagination.next_cursor` until it is
empty:

```python
from permio import raw

org = raw.organisation_pb2
page = raw.pagination_pb2.PaginationRequest(limit=100)
while True:
    res = permio.organisations.ListAPIKeys(
        org.ListAPIKeysRequest(organisation_id="your-org-id", project_name="default", pagination=page)
    )
    for key in res.api_keys:
        print(key.name)
    if not res.pagination.next_cursor:
        break
    page.cursor = res.pagination.next_cursor
```

### Raw client (full API)

`permio.permissions` and `permio.organisations` are the generated gRPC stubs for
`permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService` and `permio.organisation.v1.OrganisationService`, with authentication,
timeouts, retries (reads only) and error mapping already applied. Every RPC in the
[API reference](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/) is available. Method names are the RPC names, requests are the generated
messages with the proto field names, and each method also takes `timeout` (an overall deadline) and `metadata`. On
`AsyncPermio` they are coroutines.

The generated modules are re-exported from `permio.raw`: `permissions_pb2`, `permissions_pb2_grpc`,
`organisation_pb2`, `organisation_pb2_grpc` and `pagination_pb2`. They also live at `permio.permissions.v1`,
`permio.organisation.v1` and `permio.pagination.v1`.

```python
from permio import raw

pb = raw.permissions_pb2

permio.permissions.CreatePermission(
    pb.CreatePermissionRequest(project_name="default", name="document.read", description="Read documents")
)

role = permio.permissions.CreateRole(
    pb.CreateRoleRequest(project_name="default", name="viewer", permissions=["document.read"])  # permission names
)

permio.grant("alice", "/documents", roles=role.id)  # role IDs

res = permio.permissions.Check(
    pb.CheckPermissionRequest(
        project_name="default",
        principal_id="alice",
        resource_uris=["/documents/42"],
        permissions=["document.read"],
    )
)
print(res.passed, res.missing_permissions)
```

**Note: What a key can call**

By default an API key has **check** access: it can run checks and access queries, and read permissions, roles,
principals, assignments and groups. Creating, updating or deleting permissions, roles and groups, granting or
revoking, and changing group members needs a key with full access. See
[API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels).

For the bare stubs with no SDK behaviour, build `raw.permissions_pb2_grpc.PermissionsServiceStub(channel)` on your own
channel and send `("authorization", "Bearer <key>")` metadata yourself.

### API key helpers

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `validate_api_key(key)` | Returns `"opaque"` for `perms_` keys and `"jwt"` for legacy JWT keys. Raises `PermioConfigError` if the key is missing or malformed. |
| `is_valid_api_key(key)` | `True` if `validate_api_key` would pass. |
| `API_KEY_LENGTH` | `44`. |

These only check the shape and checksum. Only the API can tell you whether a key exists and is still valid.

### How it talks to the API

The SDK uses native gRPC over HTTP/2 through `grpcio`, with TLS for `https://` and `host:port` base URLs. The
production default connects to `api.perms.io:443`. The key is sent as `authorization: Bearer <key>` metadata, and the
client identifies itself with the user agent `permio-python/<version>`. Timeouts are passed to gRPC as per-attempt
deadlines.

---

Source: https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/

## Rust SDK

`permio` is the official Rust client for the perms.io API. It wraps the API in a few calls for asking "may this
principal do X on this resource?". It also gives you one typed error enum, retries for idempotent reads and
`Stream`s over list endpoints. The full generated API is there too, as an escape hatch.

- Needs Rust 1.88 or newer (the minimum for tonic 0.14).
- Async on Tokio. The client must be built inside a Tokio runtime.
- Talks native gRPC over HTTP/2 through [tonic](https://docs.rs/tonic), with prost-generated messages.
- TLS comes from rustls, through the `tls` feature, which is on by default.

**Note: Not on crates.io yet**

The crate is version 0.1.0 and isn't published on crates.io yet. Until it is, depend on the Git repository, as
shown below. Publishing to crates.io is coming.

### Install

```toml
[dependencies]
permio = { git = "https://github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-rust" }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
futures-util = "0.3" # only for the list streams, see Listing with streams
```

#### Features

| Feature | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tls` | on | rustls (with ring) for `https://` endpoints such as `https://api.perms.io`. It trusts the platform's certificates and the bundled webpki roots. |

Without `tls`, only `http://` endpoints work: building a client for an `https://` endpoint fails with
`Error::Config`.

### Quick start

```rust
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), permio::Error> {
    let permio = permio::Client::builder().project("default").build()?; // key from PERMIO_API_KEY

    let doc = permio::resource!("documents", 42)?; // "/documents/42"
    if permio.check("alice", "document.read", &doc).await? {
        println!("alice may read {doc}");
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

A principal that lacks the permission is a normal answer: `check` returns `Ok(false)`. It only returns `Err` when
the call itself fails, for example because of a bad key, malformed input or network trouble.

### Configuration

```rust
use std::time::Duration;

let permio = permio::Client::builder()
    .api_key(std::env::var("PERMIO_API_KEY").unwrap()) // the default source anyway
    .endpoint(permio::DEFAULT_ENDPOINT)                 // https://api.perms.io
    .project("default")
    .timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))
    .retries(3)
    .build()?;
```

`build()` checks the API key's format and checksum straight away. A mistyped or truncated key returns
`Error::Config` before any request is sent. See [API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/) for the format. The connection
itself is made lazily, on the first call.

#### Builder options

| Method | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api_key` | `impl Into<String>` | `PERMIO_API_KEY` env var | A `perms_…` key from the dashboard, or a legacy JWT key. `Error::Config` if neither is set. |
| `endpoint` | `impl Into<String>` | `DEFAULT_ENDPOINT` | API URL. Must start with `http://` or `https://`; a trailing `/` is dropped. |
| `project` | `impl Into<String>` | none | Default project for every call. Without one, calls that need a project fail with `Error::Config`. |
| `timeout` | `Duration` | 10 s (`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`) | Timeout for each attempt, also used as the connect timeout. `Duration::ZERO` disables it. |
| `retries` | `u32` | `2` | Retries for idempotent reads. Sets `max_retries` and keeps the other retry settings. |
| `retry_config` | `RetryConfig` | see [Retries and rate limits](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/#retries-and-rate-limits) | All retry settings at once. |
| `channel` | `tonic::transport::Channel` | none | Advanced: a tonic channel to use instead of connecting to `endpoint`, for example one connected to an in-process test server. Authentication, timeouts and retries still apply. |

`build()` returns `Error::Config` if the key is missing or malformed, the endpoint isn't an http(s) URL, an `https`
endpoint is used without the `tls` feature, or it's called outside a Tokio runtime.

`permio::Client::from_env("default")` is a shorthand for `Client::builder().project("default").build()`: production
endpoint, key from `PERMIO_API_KEY`.

#### Production and development

| Constant | URL |
| --- | --- |
| `permio::DEFAULT_ENDPOINT` | `https://api.perms.io` (production, the default) |
| `permio::DEV_ENDPOINT` | `https://dev-api.perms.io` (development) |

```rust
let dev = permio::Client::builder()
    .endpoint(permio::DEV_ENDPOINT)
    .project("default")
    .build()?;
```

An API key only works in the environment and project it was created in.

#### Sharing the client and switching project

`Client` is cheap to clone and safe to share between tasks. Clones share one HTTP/2 connection, so create one client
at startup and clone it where you need it.

Most helpers have no per-call project parameter. `with_project` returns a clone with another default project:

```rust
let other = permio.with_project("other-project");
```

The exceptions are `Check` and `BatchCheck`, which take `.project(...)` (see below).

The client also exposes `permio.project()` (`Option<&str>`), `permio.endpoint()` and `permio.api_key_kind()`
(`ApiKeyKind::Opaque` or `ApiKeyKind::Jwt`).

#### `who_am_i`

Describes the credential the client uses. It needs no project, so it is a good way to verify a key at startup:

```rust
let me = permio.who_am_i().await?;
println!("{:?} {:?} {:?}", me.kind, me.project, me.api_key_access);
```

`WhoAmI` has `principal_id`, `organisation_id`, `kind` (`PrincipalKind::ApiKey`, `User`, `ServiceAccount` or
`Unknown`), `project` (the project an API key belongs to), `api_key_access` (`Some(ApiKeyAccess::Check)`,
`Some(ApiKeyAccess::Full)` or `Some(ApiKeyAccess::Unknown)` for an API key, otherwise `None`) and `email`. See
[access levels](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels).

### Checking permissions

#### `check`

Returns `true` when the principal holds the permission on the resource, directly, through a role, through a group,
through an ancestor URI or through a `_` wildcard grant:

```rust
let allowed: bool = permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42").await?;
```

The arguments are `(principal, permission, resource)`, all `&str`.

#### `check_all` and `check_any`

Both take one resource and several permissions, and make a single `Check` call:

```rust
// every permission
permio.check_all("alice", ["document.read", "document.write"], "/documents/42").await?;

// at least one permission
permio.check_any("alice", ["document.admin", "document.write"], "/documents/42").await?;
```

`check_any` works out its answer from the missing list of one `Check`, so it costs the same as `check_all`.

#### `check_detailed`

For several resources, several permissions, another project, or to find out what is missing, build a `Check`:

```rust
use permio::Check;

let result = permio
    .check_detailed(
        Check::new("alice")
            .resources(["/documents/1", "/documents/2"])
            .permissions(["document.read", "document.write"]),
    )
    .await?;
// result.allowed: false
// result.missing: [MissingPermission { resource: "/documents/2", permissions: ["document.write"] }]
```

`CheckResult` has `allowed` (the principal holds **every** permission on **every** resource) and `missing`, a
`Vec<MissingPermission>` (`resource`, `permissions`) in request order, empty when `allowed` is `true`.

`Check` builder methods:

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Check::new(principal)` | The principal being checked: one of your user or service IDs, or `group:<slug>`. |
| `resource(uri)` / `resources(uris)` | Adds one or several resource URIs. Every resource is checked. |
| `permission(name)` / `permissions(names)` | Adds one or several permission names. |
| `project(name)` | Checks in this project instead of the client's default. |

Duplicates are removed before sending. A check needs 1–100 resources and 1–100 permissions, none of them empty,
or it returns `Error::Validation` without calling the API.

#### `assert` and `assert_detailed`

Return `Ok(())` when the principal is allowed and `Err(Error::Denied { .. })` when it is not. The error carries
`principal` and `missing`:

```rust
permio.assert("alice", "document.write", "/documents/1").await?;

permio.assert_detailed(Check::new("alice").permission("document.read").resource("/documents/1")).await?;
```

#### `batch_check`

`check_detailed` gives one answer for all its resources together. `batch_check` answers **each resource
separately**, which is what you need to filter a list or decide which rows get an "edit" button:

```rust
use permio::BatchCheck;

let uris = docs
    .iter()
    .map(|d| permio::resource!("documents", d.id))
    .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;

let entries = permio
    .batch_check(BatchCheck::new("alice").resources(uris).permission("document.read"))
    .await?;
let visible: Vec<&str> = entries.iter().filter(|e| e.allowed).map(|e| e.resource.as_str()).collect();
```

It returns a `Vec<BatchCheckEntry>`, one per distinct resource, in request order. Each entry has `resource`,
`allowed` (the principal holds **every** requested permission on it) and `missing` (the requested permissions it
lacks there).

`BatchCheck` has the same builder methods as `Check`. Duplicate resources are sent once. There is no upper limit on
resources: more than 100 are split into several `BatchCheck` calls, sent concurrently. Permissions are limited to
1–100.

The SDK fails closed: if the API's answer doesn't include a result for each requested resource, `batch_check`
returns `Error::Other` instead of guessing.

#### `list_access`

Answers "where may this principal use this permission, at or below `under`?". The arguments are
`(principal, permission, under)`. It follows every page and returns an `AccessScopes`:

```rust
let access = permio.list_access("alice", "document.read", "/documents").await?;

if access.covers_all {
    // alice may read everything under /documents
} else {
    let prefixes = access.to_prefixes(); // e.g. ["/documents/4", "/documents/7"]
}
```

The [Filtering lists and building share dialogs](https://docs.perms.io/guides/filtering-and-sharing/) guide shows it in context.

`AccessScopes`:

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `under` | `String` | The URI that was asked about. |
| `covers_all` | `bool` | The principal holds the permission on `under` itself, so on everything below it. `scopes` is then a single subtree scope for `under`. |
| `scopes` | `Vec<AccessScope>` | `{ uri, kind }`, ordered by URI. `kind` is `ScopeKind::Subtree`, `Pattern`, `Exact` (reserved, not returned today) or `Unknown` (a kind this SDK version doesn't know; it never matches). |
| `is_empty()` | `bool` | No access anywhere under `under`. |
| `allows(uri)` | `bool` | Whether `uri` is covered. Matches per segment: `/a/b` covers `/a/b/c` but not `/a/bc`. Malformed URIs are never allowed. |
| `to_prefixes()` | `Vec<String>` | The subtree URIs, for prefix filters. Prefixes covered by a shorter one are dropped. Pattern scopes aren't included. |
| `patterns()` | `Vec<String>` | The pattern URIs, with `_` segments. |
| `has_patterns()` | `bool` | Some scope is a pattern, so `to_prefixes()` alone doesn't cover everything. |
| `exact()` | `Vec<String>` | The exact URIs. Empty today. |
| `regex_pattern()` | `String` | One anchored regular expression matching exactly what `allows()` accepts, for PostgreSQL `~`, MongoDB `$regex` or the `regex` crate. With no scopes it is `$.^`, which matches nothing. |

**Warning**

A prefix `p` from `to_prefixes()` means `p` **and everything below it**. Filter with
`path = p OR path starts with p + "/"`, never a bare "starts with `p`", which would let `/documents/1` match
`/documents/12`. In SQL, use `starts_with(path, p || '/')` rather than `LIKE`, where `_` is a wildcard.

For a URI outside `under`, `allows()` returning `false` means "not asked", not "denied". A `_` segment in `under` is
literal. The API key needs `permission.check` on `under` and `principal.assignment.get` on the principal.

#### `who_has_access`

Answers "who has access to this resource?". It follows every page and returns a `Vec<AccessEntry>`, ordered by
principal ID:

```rust
use permio::{GrantSource, WhoHasAccess};

let entries = permio
    .who_has_access(
        WhoHasAccess::new("/documents/42")
            .permission("document.read")
            .expand_groups(true),
    )
    .await?;

for e in &entries {
    for g in &e.via {
        let source = match &g.source {
            GrantSource::Role { name, .. } => format!("role {name}"),
            GrantSource::Direct => "direct".to_string(),
            _ => "unknown".to_string(),
        };
        println!("{} on {} ({source})", e.principal, g.resource);
    }
}
```

`WhoHasAccess` builder methods:

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `WhoHasAccess::new(resource)` | The resource to look at. A `_` segment here is literal. |
| `permission(name)` | Only count grants that confer this permission, so a principal is listed exactly when a check passes for it through its own grants (or, for entries with `via_group`, through that group). Unset, any grant counts. |
| `expand_groups(bool)` | Also list every member of each listed group, once per group, with `via_group` set. |
| `page_size(n)` | Items per page, 1–100. Default 100. |

`AccessEntry` has `principal`, `is_group`, `via_group` (a group slug, or `None`) and `via`, the grants that give the
access, most specific first. Each `AccessGrant` has:

- `resource`: the URI the grant was made on (the resource, an ancestor, or a `_` wildcard URI that matches it);
- `inherited`: `true` unless the grant was made on exactly the resource;
- `match_kind`: `GrantMatch::Exact`, `Ancestor`, `Wildcard` or `Unknown`;
- `source`: `GrantSource::Role { id, name }`, `GrantSource::Direct` for directly granted permissions, or
  `GrantSource::Unknown`.

`GrantMatch` and `GrantSource` are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a `match` on them needs a `_` arm. The API key needs
`principal.list` and `principal.assignment.list` on the project.

### Granting and revoking

Build a `Grant` with the principal and resource, then add permission names, role IDs or both:

```rust
use permio::Grant;

permio.grant(Grant::new("alice", "/documents").permission("document.read")).await?;
permio.grant(Grant::new("alice", "/documents").role(role_id)).await?; // role IDs, see list_roles
permio
    .grant(Grant::new("alice", "/documents").permissions(["document.read", "document.write"]).roles([role_id]))
    .await?;

permio.revoke(Grant::new("alice", "/documents").permission("document.read")).await?;
```

- `grant` is additive: what the principal already holds there is kept. The grant also applies to every resource
  below the URI. Unknown permissions or roles return `Error::Validation`.
- `revoke` removes names from the principal's grant on **exactly** that URI and ignores names the grant doesn't
  have, so revoking twice is harmless. Grants on ancestor URIs stay, so the principal may still pass a check;
  `who_has_access` shows where access comes from.
- A `Grant` needs at least one permission or role. Empty names return `Error::Validation`.
- Both use the client's default project; use `with_project` for another one.
- Both need a key with full access, and neither is ever retried automatically.

To grant to every member of a group, use `permio::group("editors")?` as the principal (see [Groups](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/#groups)).

### Groups

A [group](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/) is a named set of principals in a project. Grant to the group's principal ID,
`group:<slug>`, and every member holds the grant. Checks include the principal's groups automatically.

#### `permio::group(slug)`

Returns the group's principal ID. It returns `Error::Validation` unless the slug is 1–64 lower-case letters, digits
and hyphens. `GROUP_PRINCIPAL_PREFIX` is `"group:"`.

```rust
use permio::Grant;

let groups = permio.groups();
groups.create("editors", Some("Can edit every document")).await?;
groups.add_members("editors", ["alice", "bob"]).await?;

permio
    .grant(Grant::new(permio::group("editors")?, "/documents").permission("document.write"))
    .await?;

permio.check("alice", "document.write", "/documents/42").await?; // true, through the group
```

#### `permio.groups()`

Returns a `Groups` handle. Every method that takes a group accepts its slug (`"editors"`) or its principal ID
(`"group:editors"`). Calls use the client's default project; use `with_project` for another one.

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `create(name, description: Option<&str>)` | `Group`. `Error::Other` with code `AlreadyExists` if the project already has a group with this name. |
| `get(name)` | `Group`. `Error::NotFound` if it doesn't exist. |
| `update(name, description: &str)` | `Group`. Replaces the description; a group can't be renamed. `Error::NotFound` if it doesn't exist. |
| `delete(name)` | `()`. Deletes the group, its memberships and every grant made to it. Succeeds whether or not it existed. |
| `list(ListOptions)` | `ListStream<Group>`, ordered by name. |
| `add_members(name, principals)` | `AddMembersResult { added, existing }`, in request order. |
| `remove_members(name, principals)` | `RemoveMembersResult { removed, not_members }`, in request order. |
| `list_members(name, ListOptions)` | `ListStream<GroupMember>` (`principal_id`, `created_at`), ordered by principal ID. |
| `list_for_principal(principal, ListOptions)` | `ListStream<Group>` of the groups the principal is a member of, ordered by name. |

- `add_members` and `remove_members` take 1–100 principals; duplicates are removed. `add_members` rejects `group:`
  IDs with `Error::Validation`, because groups can't contain groups.
- `Group` is the generated message, re-exported as `permio::Group`. It has `id`, `organisation_id`, `project_name`,
  `name`, `description`, `principal_id` (`"group:<name>"`), `created_at` and `updated_at`.

```rust
use futures_util::TryStreamExt;

let res = permio.groups().add_members("group:editors", ["alice", "carol"]).await?;
println!("added {:?}, already members {:?}", res.added, res.existing);

let mut members = permio.groups().list_members("editors", Default::default());
while let Some(m) = members.try_next().await? {
    println!("{}", m.principal_id);
}
```

Reading groups works with a check-access API key. Creating, updating and deleting groups and changing members needs
a key with full access, and changing members also needs the right to grant across the project. See
[Permissions you need](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/#permissions-you-need).

### Resource URIs

Resource URIs are paths such as `/projects/p1/documents/42`. A grant on a URI also covers every URI beneath it. See
[Resources and inheritance](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/resources/) for the full rules.

#### `resource!` and `resource()`

Build a URI from raw segments. They add the leading `/` and percent-encode each segment, so an ID that contains
`/`, spaces or other reserved characters stays a single segment. The macro takes segments of mixed `Display` types;
the function takes any iterator of one `Display` type:

```rust
permio::resource!("projects", "p1", "documents", 42)?; // "/projects/p1/documents/42"
permio::resource(["files", "reports/2026.pdf"])?;    // "/files/reports%2F2026.pdf"
```

Everything except ASCII letters, digits and `- _ . ~` is encoded, as UTF-8. Both return `Error::Validation` for an
empty segment or no segments at all.

**Tip**

Build URIs the same way when you grant and when you check, or they will not match.

#### Other helpers

| Item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `encode_segment(segment)` | Encodes one segment the way `resource()` does. |
| `validate_resource_uri(uri)` | Returns `Error::Validation` unless `uri` has the basic shape the API accepts: a leading `/`, no empty segments (so no `//`, trailing `/` or bare `/`), no whitespace or control characters, and at most 2048 bytes. |
| `MAX_RESOURCE_URI_LENGTH` | `2048`. |
| `WILDCARD_SEGMENT` | `"_"`, the segment that matches exactly one segment in a stored grant. |

Every helper runs `validate_resource_uri` on its URIs before sending. The API enforces the remaining rules, such as
no `( ) [ ] { } * + ? | ^ $ \` in segments, and answers with `InvalidArgument`, which the SDK returns as
`Error::Validation`.

### Errors

Every fallible call returns `Result<_, permio::Error>`. `Error` is an enum with one variant per kind of failure:

| Variant | When |
| --- | --- |
| `Config { message }` | Bad client setup: a missing or malformed API key, no project, an invalid endpoint, `https` without the `tls` feature, or no Tokio runtime. |
| `Auth { .. }` | `Unauthenticated`: the key is missing, unknown or invalidated. |
| `Permission { missing, .. }` | `PermissionDenied`: the **API key** lacks the rights for this call. `missing` lists what it lacks when the API says. |
| `Validation { message, status }` | `InvalidArgument`, or the SDK's own input checks (then `status` is `None`). |
| `NotFound { .. }` | `NotFound`, for example `groups().get` for a group that doesn't exist. |
| `Unavailable { .. }` | `Unavailable`, including connection and TLS failures. |
| `Timeout { .. }` | `DeadlineExceeded`, including the SDK's own per-attempt timeout. |
| `RateLimited { retry_after, .. }` | `ResourceExhausted`: the organisation's rate limit is used up. `retry_after` is the delay the server asked for, if it gave one. |
| `Denied { principal, missing, .. }` | Returned only by `assert` and `assert_detailed`, when the **principal** is not allowed. |
| `Other { message, status }` | Any other gRPC code (for example `AlreadyExists` or `Internal`), or an inconsistent API response (then `status` is `None`). |

Every variant has a `message`. The methods on `Error` are:

- `code()`: the gRPC `Code`, when the error came from the API (`None` for `Config`, `Denied` and local validation);
- `message()`: the message without the `permio: <kind>:` prefix;
- `status()`: the original `tonic::Status`;
- `metadata()`: the response headers and trailers.

`tonic` is re-exported as `permio::tonic`, so you can name `permio::tonic::Code` without adding tonic as a
dependency.

**Note: Denied is not an error**

`Error::Permission` is about the *caller*. It means your API key is not allowed to make the call: for `Check`,
the key needs `permission.check` on the checked resources and on the principal. A principal failing a check is
a normal result: `check()` returns `Ok(false)` and only `assert()` returns `Error::Denied`.

`Error::Permission`'s `missing` uses the API's fully qualified URIs (`/organisation/{org}/project/{project}/...`),
not the URIs you sent.

`Error` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a `match` needs a catch-all arm:

```rust
use permio::Error;

match permio.assert("alice", "document.write", "/documents/1").await {
    Ok(()) => { /* allowed */ }
    Err(Error::Denied { missing, .. }) => {
        // the principal may not do this: respond with 403
    }
    Err(Error::Permission { missing, .. }) => {
        // the API key may not run this check (it needs permission.check)
        eprintln!("API key lacks {missing:?}");
    }
    Err(Error::Auth { .. }) => {
        // the API key is missing, unknown or invalidated
    }
    Err(err) => eprintln!("{:?} {}", err.code(), err.message()),
}
```

`permio::Error::from(status)` converts a `tonic::Status` into the matching variant, for errors from the
[raw clients](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/#raw-clients-full-api). `parse_missing_permissions(message)` extracts the missing list from a
`PermissionDenied` message. `server_retry_delay(&status)` reads the delay a rate-limited status asks for, and
`rate_limited_status(message, delay)` builds one, for fake servers in tests.

### Retries and rate limits

- **Retries:** idempotent reads are retried on `Unavailable` and `DeadlineExceeded`, including the SDK's own
  per-attempt timeout. They are `Check`, `BatchCheck`, `ListAccess`, `ListPrincipalsWithAccess`, `WhoAmI`, the group
  reads and every other `Get*` and `List*` RPC. `permio::is_idempotent_method(name)` tells you whether a given RPC
  is retried, for example `is_idempotent_method("permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService.Check")`.
- **Backoff:** exponential with jitter. Before retry *n* (counting from 0), the SDK waits a random time between half
  and all of `min(base_delay × 2ⁿ, max_delay)`: with the defaults, 50–100 ms, then 100–200 ms.
- **Rate limits:** a rate-limited read (`ResourceExhausted`) is retried only when the server says how long to wait,
  through a `google.rpc.RetryInfo` detail or a `retry-after` header in seconds, and only if that delay is at most
  `max_delay`. The SDK then waits at least that long, plus a little jitter. Otherwise, and for every rate-limited
  write, the call returns `Error::RateLimited` with `retry_after` set when the server gave a delay. These retries
  count towards `max_retries`.
- **Writes** (every Create, Update, Delete, Grant, Revoke, adding and removing group members, and so on) are sent
  exactly once and never retried.
- **Timeouts:** the client's `timeout` applies to each attempt (default 10 s). There is no overall deadline across
  retries; wrap the call in `tokio::time::timeout` for one.

`RetryConfig`:

| Field | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_retries` | `2` | Retries after the first attempt. |
| `base_delay` | 100 ms | The delay before the first retry, which doubles each time. |
| `max_delay` | 2 s | The cap on a single delay, and on a server-requested delay the SDK will wait for. |

```rust
use std::time::Duration;

let permio = permio::Client::builder()
    .project("default")
    .timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))
```
