```rust
    .retry_config(permio::RetryConfig {
        max_retries: 3,
        base_delay: Duration::from_millis(200),
        max_delay: Duration::from_secs(5),
    })
    .build()?;

// an overall deadline of 8 s across all attempts
let allowed = tokio::time::timeout(
    Duration::from_secs(8),
    permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/1"),
)
.await;
```

`RetryConfig::none()` turns retries off.

### Listing with streams

List RPCs are paginated with a cursor (see [Pagination](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/pagination/)). The list helpers return a
`permio::ListStream<T>`, a boxed `Stream<Item = Result<T, permio::Error>>` that fetches pages lazily as you poll it.
Dropping the stream stops the listing. Use `futures_util::TryStreamExt` to consume it:

```rust
use futures_util::TryStreamExt;
use permio::ListOptions;

let mut perms = permio.list_permissions(ListOptions::default().search("document."));
while let Some(p) = perms.try_next().await? {
    println!("{}", p.name);
}

let roles: Vec<permio::Role> = permio.list_roles(Default::default()).try_collect().await?;
let principals: Vec<String> = permio.list_principals(Default::default()).try_collect().await?;

let mut assignments = permio.list_assignments("alice", Default::default());
while let Some(a) = assignments.try_next().await? {
    println!("{} {:?}", a.resource_uri, a.roles);
}
```

| Method | Yields |
| --- | --- |
| `list_permissions(options)` | `Permission` |
| `list_roles(options)` | `Role` (with its `permissions`) |
| `list_principals(options)` | `String` principal IDs that have grants in the project |
| `list_assignments(principal, options)` | `Assignment` (`resource_uri`, `permissions`, `roles`) |
| `groups().list(options)` | `Group` (see [Groups](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/#groups)) |
| `groups().list_members(name, options)` | `GroupMember` |
| `groups().list_for_principal(principal, options)` | `Group` |

`Permission`, `Role`, `Assignment`, `Group` and `GroupMember` are the generated messages, re-exported at the crate
root.

`ListOptions` has two settings:

- `page_size(n)`: items per page, clamped to 1–100 (`MAX_PAGE_SIZE`). Default 100.
- `search(text)`: filters by name, where the RPC supports it (permissions, roles, principals, groups). It is ignored
  elsewhere.

All list helpers use the client's default project; use `with_project` for another one. A configuration or input
error is returned as the stream's first item.

For any other list RPC, use `permio::paginate(page_size, fetch)`, which follows `next_cursor` until the API returns
an empty (or repeated) one:

```rust
use futures_util::TryStreamExt;
use permio::raw::organisation::v1::ListApiKeysRequest;

let raw = permio.raw_organisations();
let keys: Vec<_> = permio::paginate(100, move |pagination| {
    let mut raw = raw.clone();
    async move {
        let res = raw
            .list_api_keys(ListApiKeysRequest {
                project_name: "default".into(),
                pagination: Some(pagination),
                ..Default::default()
            })
            .await?
            .into_inner();
        Ok((res.api_keys, res.pagination))
    }
})
.try_collect()
.await?;
```

### Raw clients (full API)

`permio::raw` holds the generated prost messages and tonic clients for `permio.permissions.v1`
(`permio::raw::permissions::v1`), `permio.organisation.v1` (`permio::raw::organisation::v1`) and `pagination`
(`permio::raw::pagination`). `permio.raw_permissions()` and `permio.raw_organisations()` return a
`PermissionsServiceClient` and an `OrganisationServiceClient` that share the SDK's connection, authentication,
timeouts and retries. Every RPC in the [API reference](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/) is available. Method names are
the RPC names in snake case, and fields are the proto field names:

```rust
use permio::raw::permissions::v1::{
    CheckPermissionRequest, CreatePermissionRequest, CreateRoleRequest,
    GrantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResourceRequest,
};

let mut raw = permio.raw_permissions();

raw.create_permission(CreatePermissionRequest {
    project_name: "default".into(),
    name: "document.read".into(),
    description: "Read documents".into(),
})
.await?;

let role = raw
    .create_role(CreateRoleRequest {
        project_name: "default".into(),
        name: "viewer".into(),
        permissions: vec!["document.read".into()], // permission names
        ..Default::default()
    })
    .await?
    .into_inner();

raw.grant_user_permissions_and_roles_on_resource(GrantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResourceRequest {
    project_name: "default".into(),
    user_id: "alice".into(),
    resource_uri: "/documents".into(),
    roles: vec![role.id], // role IDs
    ..Default::default()
})
.await?;

let res = raw
    .check(CheckPermissionRequest {
        project_name: "default".into(),
        principal_id: "alice".into(),
        resource_uris: vec!["/documents/42".into()],
        permissions: vec!["document.read".into()],
    })
    .await?
    .into_inner();
println!("{} {:?}", res.passed, res.missing_permissions);
```

Raw calls return `Result<tonic::Response<T>, tonic::Status>`. In a function returning `Result<_, permio::Error>`,
`?` converts the status for you; elsewhere use `.map_err(permio::Error::from)`. The raw request types don't take a
default project: set `project_name` on every request.

**Note: What a key can call**

By default an API key has **check** access: it can run checks and access queries, and read permissions, roles,
principals, assignments and groups. Creating, updating or deleting permissions, roles and groups, granting or
revoking, and changing group members needs a key with full access. See
[API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels).

### API key helpers

| Item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `validate_api_key(key)` | Returns `ApiKeyKind::Opaque` for `perms_` keys and `ApiKeyKind::Jwt` for legacy JWT keys. Returns `Error::Config` if the key is malformed. |
| `is_valid_api_key(key)` | `true` if `validate_api_key` would pass. |
| `API_KEY_LENGTH` | `44`. |
| `API_KEY_ENV` | `"PERMIO_API_KEY"`, the variable the builder reads. |

These only check the shape and checksum. Only the API can tell you whether a key exists and is still valid; use
`who_am_i` for that.

### How it talks to the API

The SDK speaks native gRPC over HTTP/2 through tonic, not gRPC-web or REST. Every call, from the helpers and the
raw clients alike, goes through one tower service (`permio::Transport`) that adds `authorization: Bearer <key>`,
applies the per-attempt timeout and retries idempotent reads. It sends the user agent `permio-rust/<version>`.
Request and response bodies are buffered, which suits the perms.io API, where every public RPC is unary.

---

Source: https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/

## Java SDK

`io.perms:permio` is the official Java client for the perms.io API. It wraps the API in a few calls for asking "may
this principal do X on this resource?". It also gives you typed exceptions, retries for idempotent reads and lazy
iterables over list endpoints. The generated gRPC stubs for the whole API are there too, as an escape hatch.

- Runs on Java 11 or later.
- Talks gRPC over HTTP/2 with TLS, using [grpc-java](https://grpc.io/docs/languages/java/) and protobuf-java 4.
- Depends on `grpc-api`, `grpc-stub`, `grpc-protobuf`, `protobuf-java` and `pgv-java-stub`, plus
  `grpc-netty-shaded` at runtime.

**Note: Coming soon to Maven Central**

The Java SDK isn't on Maven Central yet. The coordinates below are the ones it will be published under, and they
won't resolve until then. This page describes version **0.1.0**.

### Install

**Gradle**

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("io.perms:permio:0.1.0")
}
```

**Maven**

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.perms</groupId>
  <artifactId>permio</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
</dependency>
```

### Quick start

```java
import io.perms.Permio;

// The API key is read from the PERMIO_API_KEY environment variable.
try (Permio permio = Permio.builder().project("default").build()) {
    boolean allowed = permio.check("alice", "document.read", Permio.resource("documents", 42));
}
```

The arguments are `principal`, `permission`, `resource`, in that order. They are all strings, so the compiler won't
catch them swapped round.

A principal that lacks the permission is a normal answer: `check` returns `false`. It only throws when the call itself
fails, for example because of a bad key, malformed input or network trouble.

### Configuration

```java
import io.perms.Permio;
import java.time.Duration;

Permio permio = Permio.builder()
    .apiKey(System.getenv("PERMIO_API_KEY")) // the default when not set
    .baseUrl(Permio.DEV_BASE_URL)            // default: Permio.DEFAULT_BASE_URL
    .project("default")                      // default project for every helper
    .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))          // per attempt; default 10 s
    .retries(3)                              // idempotent reads only; default 2
    .build();
```

`build()` checks the API key's format and checksum straight away. A missing, mistyped or truncated key throws
`PermioConfigException` before any request is sent. So does a malformed base URL. See
[API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/) for the key format.

`Permio.create(apiKey)` is a shortcut for a production client with no default project.

#### Options

| Builder method | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apiKey(String)` | `$PERMIO_API_KEY` | A `perms_…` key from the dashboard, or a legacy JWT key. |
| `baseUrl(String)` / `endpoint(String)` | `https://api.perms.io` | API host: `https://host[:port]` (TLS), or `http://host[:port]` (plaintext, for local testing). No path, query or fragment. |
| `project(String)` | none | Default project for every helper. Override it with `withProject` (below). |
| `timeout(Duration)` | 10 s | Timeout for each attempt. `Duration.ZERO`, or a negative duration, disables it. |
| `retries(int)` | `2` | Retries for idempotent reads. Shorthand for `retryPolicy(RetryPolicy.ofMaxRetries(n))`. |
| `retryPolicy(RetryPolicy)` | `RetryPolicy.DEFAULT` | Full retry settings; see [Retries and rate limits](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/#retries-and-rate-limits). |
| `channel(io.grpc.Channel)` | built from `baseUrl` | Advanced: a gRPC channel to use instead, for example an in-process channel in tests. `baseUrl` is then ignored. Auth, timeouts and retries still apply. The client doesn't shut it down. |
| `executor(Executor)` | a cached pool of daemon threads | Runs the `*Async` methods. An executor you pass isn't shut down by `close()`. |
| `configureChannel(Consumer<ManagedChannelBuilder<?>>)` | none | Advanced: adjust the channel builder (keepalive, proxy, interceptors) before the channel is built. Ignored when `channel` is set. |

The client has no default project. Every helper except `whoAmI()` needs one, and throws `PermioConfigException`
when there is none.

#### Production and development

| Constant | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Permio.DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | `https://api.perms.io` (production, the default) |
| `Permio.DEV_BASE_URL` | `https://dev-api.perms.io` (development) |

An API key belongs to one project in one environment, so a production key won't work against the development API.

Other constants: `Permio.API_KEY_ENV` (`"PERMIO_API_KEY"`), `Permio.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (10 s) and `Permio.VERSION`
(the SDK version, also sent in the user agent).

#### Views

`withProject(name)` and `withCallTimeout(duration)` return views of the client that share its channel:

```java
Permio billing = permio.withProject("billing");
billing.check("alice", "invoice.read", "/invoices/1");

Permio strict = permio.withCallTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(2));
```

- `withProject` uses another default project. An empty name throws `PermioConfigException`.
- `withCallTimeout` gives each call an overall deadline across all its attempts, on top of the per-attempt timeout.
  The duration must be positive. List helpers apply it to each page request.

The client also exposes `project()` (an `Optional<String>`), `baseUrl()` (`null` when you passed a channel) and
`apiKeyKind()` (`ApiKeys.Kind.OPAQUE` or `ApiKeys.Kind.JWT`).

#### Checking the key

`whoAmI()` asks the API who the key is. It is useful to verify a key at startup, and it needs no project:

```java
import io.perms.WhoAmI;

WhoAmI me = permio.whoAmI();
me.principalId();    // the key's ID
me.organisationId();
me.project();        // Optional<String>: the key's project
me.apiKeyAccess();   // Optional<WhoAmI.ApiKeyAccess>: CHECK, FULL or UNKNOWN
```

`ApiKeys.validate(key)` runs the same local format and checksum check as `build()` and returns the key's `Kind`.
`ApiKeys.isValid(key)` returns a boolean instead of throwing. `ApiKeys.API_KEY_LENGTH` is `44`. Only the API can tell
you whether a key exists and is still valid.

#### Closing the client

A `Permio` is thread-safe and owns a gRPC channel. Create one at startup, share it, and close it at shutdown.
`close()` shuts down the channel and the executors the client created, waiting up to 5 seconds for calls in flight.
A channel or executor you passed to the builder is left alone, and closing a view does nothing.

### Checking permissions

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `check(principal, permission, resource)` | `boolean`: the principal holds the permission on the resource. |
| `checkAll(principal, permissions, resources)` | `boolean`: every permission on every resource. `resources` can also be a single `String`. |
| `checkAny(principal, permissions, resources)` | `boolean`: on every resource, at least one of the permissions. `resources` can also be a single `String`. |
| `checkDetailed(principal, permissions, resources)` | `CheckResult`: the answer and what is missing. Also `checkDetailed(principal, permission, resource)`. |
| `assertAllowed(principal, permission, resource)` | Nothing; throws `PermioDeniedException` when denied. Also takes collections of permissions and resources. |

`permissions` and `resources` are `Collection<String>`s. Each takes 1–100 values; duplicates are removed before
sending. The principal must not be empty, and every resource URI is checked with
[`Resources.assertResourceUri`](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/#other-helpers) first. Breaking any of these rules throws
`PermioValidationException` without sending a request. Every check runs in the client's project.

#### `check`

```java
boolean allowed = permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42");
```

#### `checkDetailed`

Same question, but it also tells you what is missing, per resource and in request order:

```java
import io.perms.CheckResult;
import java.util.List;

CheckResult result = permio.checkDetailed(
    "alice",
    List.of("document.read", "document.write"),
    List.of("/documents/1", "/documents/2"));
result.allowed(); // false
result.missing(); // [MissingPermission{resource=/documents/2, permissions=[document.write]}]
```

`missing()` is a `List<MissingPermission>`, each with `resource()` and `permissions()`. It is empty when `allowed()`
is `true`.

#### `assertAllowed`

Returns when the principal is allowed and throws `PermioDeniedException` when it is not. The exception carries
`principal()` and `missing()`:

```java
permio.assertAllowed("alice", "document.write", "/documents/1");
```

#### `checkAny`

Returns `true` when, **on every resource**, the principal holds **at least one** of the permissions. It is still a
single API call:

```java
permio.checkAny("alice", List.of("document.admin", "document.write"), "/documents/1");
```

#### `checkAll`

Every permission on every resource, like `check` with collections:

```java
permio.checkAll("alice", List.of("document.read", "document.write"), "/documents/1");
```

### Batch checks

`check` gives one answer for all its resources together. `batchCheck` answers **each resource separately**, which is
what you need to filter a list or decide which rows get an "edit" button.

#### `batchCheck`

Returns an unmodifiable `Map<String, Boolean>` from resource URI to allowed, with one entry per distinct resource,
in request order:

```java
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

List<String> uris = docs.stream()
    .map(d -> Permio.resource("documents", d.id()))
    .collect(Collectors.toList());
Map<String, Boolean> allowed = permio.batchCheck("alice", "document.read", uris);
List<Doc> visible = docs.stream()
    .filter(d -> allowed.get(Permio.resource("documents", d.id())))
    .collect(Collectors.toList());
```

`batchCheck(principal, permissions, resources)` takes up to 100 permissions; a resource is then allowed only with
**all** of them. Duplicate resources are sent once. More than 100 resources are split into several calls, sent in
parallel.

#### `batchCheckDetailed`

Same question, but returns a `List<BatchCheckEntry>` in request order. Each entry has `resource()`, `allowed()` and
`missing()`, the permission names it lacks there:

```java
import io.perms.BatchCheckEntry;

List<BatchCheckEntry> entries = permio.batchCheckDetailed(
    "alice",
    List.of("document.read", "document.write"),
    List.of("/documents/1", "/documents/2"));
// [BatchCheckEntry{resource=/documents/1, allowed=true, missing=[]},
//  BatchCheckEntry{resource=/documents/2, allowed=false, missing=[document.write]}]
```

The SDK fails closed: if the API's answer doesn't include a result for each requested resource, it throws a
`PermioException` instead of guessing.

### Access queries

These answer "where?" and "who?" rather than "may they?". Both follow every page before returning. The
[Filtering lists and building share dialogs](https://docs.perms.io/guides/filtering-and-sharing/) guide shows them in context.

#### `listAccess`

`listAccess(principal, permission, under)` answers "where may this principal use this permission, at or below
`under`?". Access through roles and groups counts. It returns an `AccessScopes`:

```java
import io.perms.AccessScopes;

AccessScopes access = permio.listAccess("alice", "document.read", "/documents");

if (access.coversAll()) {
    // alice may read everything under /documents
} else {
    System.out.println(access.toPrefixes()); // e.g. [/documents/4, /documents/7]
}
```

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `under()` | `String` | The URI that was asked about. |
| `coversAll()` | `boolean` | The principal holds the permission on `under` itself, so on everything below it. `scopes()` is then a single subtree scope for `under`. |
| `scopes()` | `List<AccessScopes.Scope>` | Each has `uri()` and `kind()`, ordered by URI. `Kind` is `SUBTREE`, `PATTERN`, `EXACT` (reserved, not returned today) or `UNKNOWN` (a kind this SDK version doesn't know; it never matches). |
| `isEmpty()` | `boolean` | No access anywhere under `under`. |
| `allows(uri)` | `boolean` | Whether `uri` is covered. Matches per segment: `/a/b` covers `/a/b/c` but not `/a/bc`. Malformed URIs are never allowed. |
| `toPrefixes()` | `List<String>` | The subtree URIs, for prefix filters. Prefixes covered by a shorter one are dropped. Pattern scopes aren't included. |
| `patterns()` | `List<String>` | The pattern URIs, with `_` segments. |
| `hasPatterns()` | `boolean` | Some scope is a pattern, so `toPrefixes()` alone doesn't cover everything. |
| `exact()` | `List<String>` | The exact URIs. Empty today. |
| `toRegex()` | `String` | One anchored regular expression matching exactly what `allows()` accepts. Usable in MongoDB `$regex` and PostgreSQL `~`. Matches nothing when there are no scopes. |
| `toPattern()` | `java.util.regex.Pattern` | `toRegex()`, compiled. |

**Warning**

A prefix `p` from `toPrefixes()` means `p` **and everything below it**. Filter with
`path = p OR path starts with p + "/"`, never a bare "starts with `p`", which would let `/documents/1` match
`/documents/12`. In SQL, use `starts_with(path, p || '/')` rather than `LIKE`, where `_` is a wildcard.

For a URI outside `under`, `allows()` returning `false` means "not asked", not "denied". The API key needs
`permission.check` on `under` and `principal.assignment.get` on the principal.

#### `whoHasAccess`

Answers "who has access to this resource?". It returns a `List<AccessEntry>`, ordered by principal ID:

```java
import io.perms.AccessEntry;

List<AccessEntry> entries = permio.whoHasAccess("/documents/42", "document.read", true);
for (AccessEntry e : entries) {
    System.out.println(e.principal() + " " + e.viaGroup().orElse("") + " " + e.via());
}
```

`whoHasAccess(resource)` counts any grant. `whoHasAccess(resource, permission, expandGroups)` takes:

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `resource` | The resource to look at. A `_` segment here is literal. |
| `permission` | Only count grants that confer this permission, so a principal is listed exactly when `check` passes for it through its own grants (or, for entries with `viaGroup`, through that group). `null` counts any grant. |
| `expandGroups` | Also list every member of each listed group, once per group, with `viaGroup` set. |

`AccessEntry` has `principal()`, `isGroup()`, `viaGroup()` (an `Optional<String>` group slug) and `via()`, the
grants that give the access, most specific first. Each grant (`AccessGrantInfo`) has:

- `resource()`: the URI the grant was made on (the resource, an ancestor, or a `_` wildcard URI that matches it);
- `inherited()`: `true` unless the grant was made on exactly the resource;
- `match()`: `EXACT`, `ANCESTOR`, `WILDCARD` or `UNKNOWN`;
- `source()`: `ROLE`, `DIRECT` (directly granted permissions) or `UNKNOWN`, with `roleId()` and `roleName()` as
  `Optional<String>`s for roles.

The API key needs `principal.list` and `principal.assignment.list` on the project.

### Async variants

These methods return a `CompletableFuture` and run on the client's executor:

| Method | Completes with |
| --- | --- |
| `checkAsync(principal, permission, resource)` | `Boolean` |
| `checkDetailedAsync(principal, permissions, resources)` | `CheckResult` |
| `batchCheckAsync(principal, permission, resources)` | `Map<String, Boolean>` |
| `listAccessAsync(principal, permission, under)` | `AccessScopes` |
| `whoHasAccessAsync(resource, permission, expandGroups)` | `List<AccessEntry>` |
| `grantAsync(grant)` / `revokeAsync(grant)` | `Void` |
| `whoAmIAsync()` | `WhoAmI` |

A failed future completes exceptionally with the same exception types as the blocking methods. `join()` and `get()`
wrap them in `CompletionException` and `ExecutionException`; `PermioException.from(e)` unwraps both.

### Granting and revoking

Grants need an API key with full access, and are sent once: they are never retried automatically.

```java
import io.perms.Grant;

permio.grant("alice", "document.read", "/documents");

permio.grant(Grant.to("alice").on("/documents").permissions("document.read").roles(roleId));
permio.revoke(Grant.to("alice").on("/documents").roles(roleId));
```

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `grant(principal, permission, resource)` | Grants one permission. |
| `grant(Grant)` | Grants permissions and roles to a principal on a resource, and so on everything below it. Additive: what the principal already holds is kept. |
| `revoke(principal, permission, resource)` | Revokes one permission. |
| `revoke(Grant)` | Removes permissions and roles from the principal's grant on exactly the resource. Names the grant doesn't hold are ignored. |

`Grant` is immutable; each method returns a copy:

- `Grant.to(principal)` starts a grant. Use `Permio.group("editors")` to grant to a group.
- `on(resource)` sets the resource URI.
- `permissions(...)` adds permission **names**, as varargs or a `Collection<String>`.
- `roles(...)` adds role **IDs**, as varargs or a `Collection<String>`.

A grant needs at least one permission or role, or it throws `PermioValidationException`. So does a permission or role
that doesn't exist in the project (the API answers `INVALID_ARGUMENT`).

**Note: Revoking doesn't touch ancestors**

`revoke` only changes the grant on exactly the URI you pass. Grants on ancestor URIs, or on `_` wildcard URIs
that match it, are kept, so the principal may still pass `check` afterwards. `whoHasAccess` shows where access
comes from.

### Groups

A [group](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/) is a named set of principals in a project. Grant to the group's principal ID,
`group:<slug>`, and every member holds the grant. Checks include the principal's groups automatically.

#### `Permio.group(slug)`

Returns the group's principal ID. It throws `PermioValidationException` unless the slug is 1–64 lower-case letters,
digits and hyphens. `Groups.principal(slug)` does the same, and `Groups.GROUP_PRINCIPAL_PREFIX` is `"group:"`.

```java
import io.perms.Grant;
import io.perms.Permio;

Permio.group("editors"); // "group:editors"

permio.groups().create("editors", "Can edit every document");
permio.groups().addMembers("editors", List.of("alice", "bob"));
permio.grant(Grant.to(Permio.group("editors")).on("/documents").permissions("document.write"));

permio.check("alice", "document.write", "/documents/42"); // true
```

#### `permio.groups()`

Every method that takes a group accepts its slug (`"editors"`) or its principal ID (`"group:editors"`). Groups use the
client's project.

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `create(name)` / `create(name, description)` | `Group`. Throws a `PermioException` with code `ALREADY_EXISTS` if the project already has a group with this name. |
| `get(name)` | `Group`. Throws `PermioNotFoundException` if it doesn't exist. |
| `update(name, description)` | `Group`. Replaces the description; a group can't be renamed. Throws `PermioNotFoundException` if it doesn't exist. |
| `delete(name)` | Nothing. Deletes the group, its memberships and every grant made to it. Succeeds whether or not it existed. |
| `list()` / `list(ListOptions)` | `PagedIterable<Group>`, ordered by name. Takes a search filter. |
| `addMembers(name, principals)` | `AddMembersResult`: `added()` and `existing()`, in request order. |
| `removeMembers(name, principals)` | `RemoveMembersResult`: `removed()` and `notMembers()`, in request order. |
| `listMembers(name)` | `PagedIterable<GroupMember>` (`getPrincipalId()`, `getCreatedAt()`), ordered by principal ID. |
| `listForPrincipal(principal)` | `PagedIterable<Group>`: the groups the principal is a member of, ordered by name. |

- `addMembers` and `removeMembers` take 1–100 principals; duplicates are removed. `addMembers` rejects `group:` IDs
  with `PermioValidationException`, because groups can't contain groups.
- `listMembers` and `listForPrincipal` also take a `ListOptions` for the page size.
- `Group` and `GroupMember` are the generated protobuf messages from `io.perms.proto.permissions.v1`. `Group` has
  `getId()`, `getOrganisationId()`, `getProjectName()`, `getName()`, `getDescription()`, `getPrincipalId()`
  (`"group:<name>"`), `getCreatedAt()` and `getUpdatedAt()`.
- The group methods have no async variants.

```java
import io.perms.AddMembersResult;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.Group;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.GroupMember;

AddMembersResult res = permio.groups().addMembers("group:editors", List.of("alice", "carol"));
res.added();    // [carol]
res.existing(); // [alice]

for (GroupMember m : permio.groups().listMembers("editors")) System.out.println(m.getPrincipalId());
for (Group g : permio.groups().listForPrincipal("alice")) System.out.println(g.getName());
```

Reading groups works with a check-access API key. Creating, updating and deleting groups and changing members needs
a key with full access, and changing members also needs the right to grant across the project. See
[Permissions you need](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/#permissions-you-need).

### Resource URIs

Resource URIs are paths such as `/projects/p1/documents/42`. A grant on a URI also covers every URI beneath it. See
[Resources and inheritance](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/resources/) for the full rules.

#### `Permio.resource(segments...)`

Builds a URI from raw segments. It adds the leading `/` and percent-encodes each segment, so an ID that contains `/`,
spaces or other reserved characters stays a single segment. Each segment is converted with `String.valueOf`, so
numbers and other objects work too:

```java
Permio.resource("projects", "p1", "documents", 42); // "/projects/p1/documents/42"
Permio.resource("files", "reports/2026.pdf");       // "/files/reports%2F2026.pdf"
```

Every character except `A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~` is encoded as UTF-8 bytes. This matches the TypeScript SDK's
`resource()`, so both build the same URIs. A null or empty segment, or no segments at all, throws
`PermioValidationException`. `Resources.resource(...)` is the same method.

**Tip**

Build URIs the same way when you grant and when you check, or they will not match.

#### Other helpers

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Resources.encodeSegment(segment)` | Encodes one segment the way `resource()` does. |
| `Resources.assertResourceUri(uri)` | Throws `PermioValidationException` unless `uri` has the basic shape the API accepts: a leading `/`, no empty segments, no whitespace or control characters, and at most 2048 bytes. |
| `Resources.MAX_RESOURCE_URI_LENGTH` | `2048`. |

Every check, access query and grant runs `assertResourceUri` on its URIs before sending. The API enforces the
remaining rules, such as no `( ) [ ] { } * + ? | ^ $ \` in segments, and answers with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, which the
SDK throws as `PermioValidationException`.

### Errors

Every exception the SDK throws is an unchecked `PermioException`. It has:

- `code()`: the gRPC `Status.Code`, as an `Optional`. Empty when the error didn't come from the API.
- `codeName()`: the code's name in lower case, for example `"permission_denied"`, as an `Optional`.
- `metadata()`: the response headers and trailers.
- `getCause()`: the original exception, usually a `StatusRuntimeException`.

| Exception | When |
| --- | --- |
| `PermioConfigException` | Bad client setup: a missing or malformed API key, an invalid base URL, or no project. |
| `PermioAuthException` | `UNAUTHENTICATED`: the key is missing, unknown or invalidated. |
| `PermioPermissionException` | `PERMISSION_DENIED`: the **API key** lacks the rights for this call. `missing()` lists what it lacks when the API says. |
| `PermioValidationException` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, or the SDK's own input checks (then no request is sent and `code()` is empty). |
| `PermioNotFoundException` | `NOT_FOUND`, for example `groups().get` for a group that doesn't exist. |
| `PermioUnavailableException` | `UNAVAILABLE`, including network failures, after any retries. |
| `PermioTimeoutException` | `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, including the SDK's own timeouts. |
| `PermioRateLimitException` | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`. `retryAfter()` is the delay the server asked for, as an `Optional<Duration>`. |
| `PermioDeniedException` | Thrown only by `assertAllowed`, when the **principal** is not allowed. Has `principal()` and `missing()`. |

Any other status, such as `ALREADY_EXISTS` or `INTERNAL`, is a plain `PermioException` with the matching code.

**Note: Denied is not an error**

`PermioPermissionException` is about the *caller*. It means your API key is not allowed to make the call: for
`Check`, the key needs `permission.check` on the checked resources and on the principal. A principal failing a
check is a normal result: `check` returns `false` and `assertAllowed` throws `PermioDeniedException`.

`PermioPermissionException.missing()` uses the API's fully qualified URIs (`/organisation/{org}/project/{project}/...`),
not the URIs you sent.

```java
import io.perms.PermioAuthException;
import io.perms.PermioDeniedException;
import io.perms.PermioException;
import io.perms.PermioPermissionException;

try {
    permio.assertAllowed("alice", "document.write", "/documents/1");
} catch (PermioDeniedException e) {
    // the principal may not do this: respond with 403
} catch (PermioPermissionException e) {
    // the API key may not run this check (it needs permission.check)
    System.err.println(e.missing());
} catch (PermioAuthException e) {
    // the API key is missing, unknown or invalidated
} catch (PermioException e) {
    System.err.println(e.codeName().orElse("error") + ": " + e.getMessage());
}
```

`PermioException.from(throwable)` converts any exception into the matching subclass. It unwraps
`ExecutionException` and `CompletionException`, and maps gRPC status exceptions by code. Anything else becomes a plain
`PermioException` with code `UNKNOWN`. `PermioException.parseMissingPermissions(message)` extracts the missing list
from a `PERMISSION_DENIED` message. You only need these with the [raw client](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/#raw-client).

### Retries and rate limits

- **Retries:** idempotent reads are retried on `UNAVAILABLE` and `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. These are `Check`,
  `BatchCheck`, `WhoAmI` and the `Get*` and `List*` RPCs, including `ListAccess`, `ListPrincipalsWithAccess`, the
  group reads and the read-only organisation calls. By default they are retried twice, with exponential backoff and
  jitter. Network failures count as `UNAVAILABLE`.
- **Writes** (every Create, Update, Delete, Grant, Revoke, Invite, adding and removing group members, and so on) are
  sent exactly once. After a timeout the first attempt may still have landed, and repeating it could undo another
  caller's change. Retry them yourself if that is safe for you.
- **Backoff:** the delay before retry *n* is a random value between half and all of
  `min(maxDelay, baseDelay × 2^(n−1))`. If the server sends a `retry-after` header with `UNAVAILABLE`, the SDK waits
  at least that long, or doesn't retry when it is longer than `maxDelay`.
- **Rate limits:** a read that fails with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` is retried only when the server says how long to wait
  (a `google.rpc.RetryInfo` error detail, or a `retry-after` header) and that delay is within `maxDelay`. The SDK
  then waits at least that long, plus up to 100 ms of jitter. Otherwise it throws `PermioRateLimitException` with
  `retryAfter()` set. Writes are never retried, whatever the code.
- **Timeouts:**
    - The builder's `timeout` applies to each attempt (default 10 s).
    - `withCallTimeout`, or a deadline you set on a raw stub, is an overall deadline across all attempts. If it would
      expire before the next retry, the call fails with `PermioTimeoutException` straight away.

```java
import io.perms.RetryPolicy;

Permio permio = Permio.builder()
    .project("default")
    .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
    .retryPolicy(RetryPolicy.builder()
        .maxRetries(3)
        .baseDelay(Duration.ofMillis(100))
        .maxDelay(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
        .build())
    .build();
```

`RetryPolicy` has these settings:

- `maxRetries`: retries after the first attempt. Default 2. Negative values count as 0.
- `baseDelay`: the first delay, which doubles each time. Default 100 ms.
- `maxDelay`: the cap on a single delay, and on a server-requested delay the SDK will wait. Default 2 s.

`RetryPolicy.DEFAULT` holds the defaults and `RetryPolicy.NONE` turns retries off.
`RetryPolicy.isIdempotent("permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService/Check")` tells you whether the SDK retries a given
RPC. The dotted form, `permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService.Check`, works too.

To back off from a rate limit yourself:

```java
import io.perms.PermioRateLimitException;

try {
    permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42");
} catch (PermioRateLimitException e) {
    Duration wait = e.retryAfter().orElse(Duration.ofSeconds(1));
    // try again after `wait`
}
```

### Listing with iterators

List RPCs are paginated with a cursor (see [Pagination](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/pagination/)). The list helpers return a
`PagedIterable<T>`, which fetches pages lazily as you iterate:

```java
import io.perms.ListOptions;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.Assignment;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.Permission;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.Role;

for (Permission p : permio.listPermissions(ListOptions.defaults().withSearch("document."))) {
    System.out.println(p.getName());
}
for (Role role : permio.listRoles()) System.out.println(role.getName() + " " + role.getPermissionsCount());
for (String id : permio.listPrincipals()) System.out.println(id);
for (Assignment a : permio.listGrants("alice")) System.out.println(a.getResourceUri() + " " + a.getRolesList());

List<String> principals = permio.listPrincipals().toList();
long roles = permio.listRoles().stream().count();
```

| Method | Yields |
| --- | --- |
| `listPermissions()` / `listPermissions(ListOptions)` | `Permission` |
| `listRoles()` / `listRoles(ListOptions)` | `Role` (with its permissions) |
| `listPrincipals()` / `listPrincipals(ListOptions)` | `String` principal IDs that have grants in the project |
| `listGrants(principal)` / `listGrants(principal, ListOptions)` | `Assignment` (`getResourceUri()`, `getPermissionsList()`, `getRolesList()`). `listAssignments(principal)` is an alias. |
| `groups().list(...)`, `groups().listMembers(...)`, `groups().listForPrincipal(...)` | See [Groups](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/#groups). |

The items are the generated protobuf messages from `io.perms.proto.permissions.v1`.

`ListOptions` is immutable:

- `ListOptions.defaults()`: no search filter, 100 items per page.
- `withSearch(text)`: filters by name. It applies to `listPermissions`, `listRoles`, `listPrincipals` and
  `groups().list`; the other list methods ignore it.
- `withPageSize(n)`: items per page, clamped to 1–100.

`PagedIterable` is an `Iterable`, and also has `stream()` and `toList()` (which fetches every page). Each new
iteration or stream starts again from the first page. Iteration stops when the API returns an empty cursor, or one it
has already returned. API errors are thrown from `hasNext()` as `PermioException`s.

For any other list RPC, build a `PagedIterable` yourself. It passes you a `PaginationRequest`; you return a
`PagedIterable.Page` with the items and the next cursor:

```java
import io.perms.PagedIterable;
import io.perms.proto.organisation.v1.APIKey;
import io.perms.proto.organisation.v1.ListAPIKeysRequest;
import io.perms.proto.organisation.v1.ListAPIKeysResponse;

PagedIterable<APIKey> keys = new PagedIterable<>(
    page -> {
        ListAPIKeysResponse res = permio.raw().organisations().listAPIKeys(
            ListAPIKeysRequest.newBuilder()
                .setOrganisationId("your-org-id")
                .setProjectName("default")
                .setPagination(page)
                .build());
        return new PagedIterable.Page<>(res.getApiKeysList(), res.getPagination().getNextCursor());
    },
    100);
for (APIKey key : keys) System.out.println(key.getName());
```

### Raw client

`permio.raw()` returns a `RawClient` with the generated [grpc-java](https://grpc.io/docs/languages/java/) stubs for
`permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService` and `permio.organisation.v1.OrganisationService`. They run over the
client's channel, so authentication, timeouts and retries already apply. Every RPC in the
[API reference](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/) is available. Method names are the RPC names in lower camel case, and the
request builders use camelCase setters:

| Method | Stub |
| --- | --- |
| `permissions()` | `PermissionsServiceGrpc.PermissionsServiceBlockingStub` |
| `permissionsFuture()` | `PermissionsServiceGrpc.PermissionsServiceFutureStub` (`ListenableFuture`) |
| `permissionsAsync()` | `PermissionsServiceGrpc.PermissionsServiceStub` (`StreamObserver`) |
| `organisations()`, `organisationsFuture()`, `organisationsAsync()` | The same three for `OrganisationServiceGrpc` |
| `channel()` | The client's `io.grpc.Channel`, for building any stub yourself |

```java
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.CheckPermissionRequest;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.CheckPermissionResponse;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.CreatePermissionRequest;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.CreateRoleRequest;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.GrantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResourceRequest;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.Role;

var stub = permio.raw().permissions();

stub.createPermission(CreatePermissionRequest.newBuilder()
    .setProjectName("default")
    .setName("document.read")
    .setDescription("Read documents")
    .build());

Role role = stub.createRole(CreateRoleRequest.newBuilder()
    .setProjectName("default")
    .setName("viewer")
    .addPermissions("document.read") // permission names
    .build());

stub.grantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource(GrantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResourceRequest.newBuilder()
    .setProjectName("default")
    .setUserId("alice")
    .setResourceUri("/documents")
    .addRoles(role.getId()) // role IDs
    .build());

CheckPermissionResponse res = stub.check(CheckPermissionRequest.newBuilder()
    .setProjectName("default")
    .setPrincipalId("alice")
    .addResourceUris("/documents/42")
    .addPermissions("document.read")
    .build());
System.out.println(res.getPassed() + " " + res.getMissingPermissionsList());
```

- Raw requests don't use the client's default project: set `project_name` on each one.
- Raw errors are plain `io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException`s. Convert them with `PermioException.from(e)` to get the
  typed exceptions above.
- On a `withCallTimeout` view, the raw stubs carry that deadline too.
- The generated messages live in `io.perms.proto.permissions.v1`, `io.perms.proto.organisation.v1` and
  `io.perms.proto.pagination.v1`.

**Note: What a key can call**

By default an API key has **check** access: it can run checks and access queries, and read permissions, roles,
principals, assignments and groups. Creating, updating or deleting permissions, roles and groups, granting or
revoking, and changing group members needs a key with full access. See
[API keys](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels).

---

Source: https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/

## API overview

The perms.io API has two services:

| Service | Proto | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Permissions](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/) | `permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService` | Permissions, roles, grants and **checks**. This is the service your application calls. |
| [Organisations](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/organizations/) | `permio.organisation.v1.OrganisationService` | Organisations, projects, API keys and team members. Mostly used by the dashboard. |

Both are defined in Permio's protobuf definitions. The same host serves them as REST/JSON, gRPC and gRPC-web.

(See "API hosts" earlier in this file.)

### Protocols

| Protocol | How to call it |
| --- | --- |
| **REST/JSON** | The HTTP method and path listed for each RPC in this reference, for example `POST $PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/check`. Request bodies accept the proto field names (`project_name`). Responses use camelCase JSON names (`missingPermissions`) and leave out fields that have default values. |
| **gRPC** | Connect to the host on port 443 with TLS, for example `api.perms.io:443`, and send the key as `authorization` metadata. The [Go](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/go/), [Python](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/), [Rust](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/) and [Java](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/) SDKs use it. |
| **gRPC-web** | The protocol the [TypeScript SDK](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/typescript/) uses. It works from servers, edge runtimes and browsers. |

For `GET` and `DELETE` requests over REST, fields that aren't in the path go in the query string. Nested fields use
dot notation, for example `?project_name=default&pagination.limit=50`.

### Authentication

Every request needs an [API key](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/), sent as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer perms_...
```

Keys are 44 characters long: `perms_`, 32 random base62 characters and a 6-character checksum. A key is shown once,
when you create it in the dashboard. Only a hash of it is stored, and you can invalidate it at any time. Older JWT
API keys are still accepted.

A key acts within its own **project**. Your organisation is worked out from the key, so permission requests don't
include an organisation ID. A key gets its own grants on its project: by default **check** access, which allows
`Check`, the access queries and the read-only calls. See [Access levels](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels).

### Errors

A **denied check is not an error**. `Check` returns success with `passed: false` and a list of
`missing_permissions`. Errors mean that the request itself could not be carried out:

| gRPC status | HTTP | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (3) | 400 | Malformed input: an invalid resource URI, an empty permissions list, a bad project name, more than 100 items in a check, and so on. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` (16) | 401 | The API key is missing, malformed, unknown or invalidated. |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` (7) | 403 | The **API key** isn't allowed to make this call. For example, a key without `permission.check` calling `Check`, or a check-only key creating a role. The message lists what is missing. |
| `NOT_FOUND` (5) | 404 | The permission, role, group or other entity doesn't exist. Also returned when a `group:<slug>` principal names a group that doesn't exist. |
| `ALREADY_EXISTS` (6) | 409 | A group with this name already exists in the project. |
| `INTERNAL` (13) | 500 | Something went wrong on our side. |
| `UNAVAILABLE` (14) | 503 | The service is temporarily unavailable. Safe to retry for reads. |

Over REST, the error body carries the gRPC code and a message:

```json
{"code": 16, "message": "invalid api key"}
```

Over gRPC and gRPC-web, the code arrives as `grpc-status` and the text as `grpc-message`.

### Clients

Official SDKs:

| Language | Package | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [TypeScript](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/typescript/) | `permio` on npm | Released |
| [Go](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/go/) | `github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go` | Untagged; the first release will be v0.1.0 |
| [Python](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/) | `permio` on PyPI | Released (0.1.0) |
| [Rust](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/) | `permio` crate | Install from Git; crates.io coming soon |
| [Java](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/) | `io.perms:permio` | Coming soon to Maven Central |

**TypeScript**

The [TypeScript SDK](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/typescript/) (`npm install permio`) is the recommended client.
Besides the check helpers, it exposes every RPC on this page through `permio.permissions` and
`permio.organisations`.

**cURL**

Every RPC has a REST path, listed with each method in this reference.

```bash
curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/check" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "principal_id": "alice", "resource_uris": ["/documents/42"], "permissions": ["document.read"]}'
```

**Go**

The [Go SDK](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/go/) (`go get github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go@latest`, Go 1.24+) is the recommended client.
Besides the check helpers, it exposes every RPC on this page through `client.Permissions()` and
`client.Organisations()`, the generated gRPC clients with auth, timeouts, retries and typed errors applied.

```go
import permio "github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-go"

client, err := permio.New(permio.Options{
    APIKey:  os.Getenv("PERMIO_API_KEY"),
    Project: "default",
})
// handle err
defer client.Close()

allowed, err := client.Check(ctx, "alice", "document.read", "/documents/42")
```

**Python**

The [Python SDK](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/) (`pip install permio`) gives you a synchronous `Permio` client and an asyncio
`AsyncPermio` client with the same methods. Besides the check helpers, both expose every RPC on this page through
`permio.permissions` and `permio.organisations`, with the generated messages in `permio.raw`.

```python
from permio import Permio

permio = Permio(api_key=api_key, project="default")  # api_key defaults to $PERMIO_API_KEY

permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42")  # True or False
```

**Rust**

The [Rust SDK](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/) (crate `permio`) is the recommended client. It isn't on crates.io yet, so depend on
the Git repository. Besides the check helpers, it exposes every RPC on this page through `permio.raw_permissions()`
and `permio.raw_organisations()`, with authentication, timeouts and retries already applied.

```toml
[dependencies]
permio = { git = "https://github.com/PrivateJAR/permio-rust" }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
```

```rust
let permio = permio::Client::builder()
    .api_key(api_key) // defaults to the PERMIO_API_KEY env var
    .project("default")
    .build()?;

let allowed = permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42").await?;
```

**Java**

The [Java SDK](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/) (`io.perms:permio`, Java 11+) wraps the check, access-query, grant and group RPCs, and
exposes every RPC on this page as generated gRPC stubs through `permio.raw()`. It is coming soon to Maven Central.

```java
import io.perms.Permio;

Permio permio = Permio.builder()
    .apiKey(System.getenv("PERMIO_API_KEY"))
    .project("default")
    .build();

boolean allowed = permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42");
```

Field names in this reference are the proto names (`project_name`). The generated clients use their language's
convention: `ProjectName` in Go, `project_name` in Python and Rust, `projectName` in TypeScript, and
`setProjectName` / `getProjectName` in Java.

#### Other languages

Permio is a gRPC and REST/JSON API, so you can use it from any language:

- **Generate a client** from Permio's public protobuf definitions with your language's gRPC tooling. The public
  protos repository is coming soon.
- **Call the REST API** with any HTTP client, using the paths listed for each RPC in this reference and the
  `Authorization: Bearer` header described in [Authentication](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/#authentication).

---

Source: https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/

## Permissions & Roles

`permio.permissions.v1.PermissionsService` stores permissions, roles and grants, and answers checks. Every request
names a `project_name`. Your organisation comes from the API key.

(See "API hosts" earlier in this file.)

In the tables below, **Key access** is the [API key access level](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/api-keys/#access-levels) needed to
make the call. **Check** is the default for new keys, and **Full** is the level that also allows writes.

| RPC | REST | Key access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Check](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#check) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/check` | Check |
| [BatchCheck](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#batchcheck) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/check/batch` | Check |
| [CreatePermission](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#createpermission) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions` | Full |
| [GetPermission](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#getpermission) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/{name}` | Check |
| [UpdatePermission](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#updatepermission) | `PUT /permissions-service/v1/permissions/{name}` | Full |
| [DeletePermission](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#deletepermission) | `DELETE /permissions-service/v1/permissions/{name}` | Full |
| [ListPermissions](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listpermissions) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions` | Check |
| [CreateRole](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#createrole) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/roles` | Full |
| [GetRole](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#getrole) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/roles/{id}` | Check |
| [UpdateRole](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#updaterole) | `PUT /permissions-service/v1/roles/{id}` | Full |
| [DeleteRole](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#deleterole) | `DELETE /permissions-service/v1/roles/{id}` | Full |
| [ListRoles](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listroles) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/roles` | Check |
| [GrantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#grantuserpermissionsandrolesonresource) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/assign` | Full |
| [RevokeUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#revokeuserpermissionsandrolesonresource) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/revoke` | Full |
| [GetUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#getuserpermissionsandrolesonresource) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/user/{user_id}/resource/{resource_uri=**}` | Check |
| [ListPrincipals](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listprincipals) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/principals` | Check |
| [GetAllAssignmentsForPrincipal](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#getallassignmentsforprincipal) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/assignments/principal/{principal_id=**}` | Check |
| [ListAccess](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listaccess) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/access` | Check |
| [ListPrincipalsWithAccess](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listprincipalswithaccess) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/access/principals` | Check |
| [CreateGroup](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#creategroup) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/groups` | Full |
| [GetGroup](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#getgroup) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}` | Check |
| [UpdateGroup](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#updategroup) | `PUT /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}` | Full |
| [DeleteGroup](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#deletegroup) | `DELETE /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}` | Full |
| [ListGroups](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listgroups) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/groups` | Check |
| [AddGroupMembers](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#addgroupmembers) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}/members/add` | Full |
| [RemoveGroupMembers](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#removegroupmembers) | `POST /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}/members/remove` | Full |
| [ListGroupMembers](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listgroupmembers) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/groups/{name}/members` | Check |
| [ListGroupsForPrincipal](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listgroupsforprincipal) | `GET /permissions-service/v1/group-memberships/{principal_id=**}` | Check |

`GetTotalRolesAndPermissionsForOrganisation` (`GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/organisation/{organisation_id}/totals`)
is also part of the service. It needs an organisation-level permission that API keys don't have, and the dashboard
uses it.

### Common field rules

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `project_name` | 1–32 characters: lowercase letters, digits and `-`. |
| Permission `name` | 1–128 characters: `a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ -`. |
| Role `name` | 1–128 characters, no control characters. |
| Role `id` | 1–128 characters: `a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ -`. |
| Group `name` | 1–64 characters: lowercase letters, digits and `-`. Its principal ID is `group:<name>`. |
| Principal IDs | Any non-empty string. IDs starting with `group:` are reserved for [groups](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/): such an ID must name a group that exists in the project, or the call fails with `NOT_FOUND` (`INVALID_ARGUMENT` if it isn't a valid group name). Revoking is the exception. |
| Resource URIs | See [Resources and inheritance](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/resources/#rules-for-uris). |

### Messages

**Permission**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique ID. |
| `organisation_id` | string | Owning organisation. |
| `name` | string | The name your code checks, e.g. `document.read`. |
| `description` | string | Free text. |
| `project_name` | string | Owning project. |

**Role**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique ID. Use it when granting and in the role endpoints. |
| `organisation_id` | string | Owning organisation. |
| `name` | string | Display name. |
| `description` | string | Free text. |
| `permissions` | Permission[] | The permissions in the role. |
| `project_name` | string | Owning project. |

**Assignment**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource_uri` | string | The resource the grant is on. |
| `permissions` | Permission[] | Permissions granted directly. |
| `roles` | Role[] | Roles granted. |

### Check

`POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/check`

Checks whether a principal holds **every** listed permission on **every** listed resource. Grants on ancestors of a
resource count, and so do grants to the [groups](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/) the principal is a member of. See
[how a check is decided](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/resources/#how-a-check-is-decided). To get one answer per resource, use
[BatchCheck](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#batchcheck).

**Request** (`CheckPermissionRequest`)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. Project to check in. |
| `principal_id` | string | Required. The principal being checked. |
| `resource_uris` | string[] | Required. 1–100 unique resource URIs. |
| `permissions` | string[] | Required. 1–100 unique permission names. |

**Response** (`CheckPermissionResponse`)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `passed` | bool | `true` if every permission is held on every resource. |
| `missing_permissions` | MissingPermissions[] | For each resource that failed: `resource_uri` and the `missing_permissions` not held there. |

A failed check is a successful response with `passed: false`. `PERMISSION_DENIED` means the **API key** lacks
`permission.check` on the resources or on the principal, not that the principal was denied.

**TypeScript**

```ts
const { allowed, missing } = await permio.checkDetailed({
  principal: "alice",
  resources: ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"],
  permission: "document.read",
});
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/check" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "project_name": "default",
    "principal_id": "alice",
    "resource_uris": ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"],
    "permissions": ["document.read"]
  }'
```

```json
{"missingPermissions": [{"resourceUri": "/invoices/1", "missingPermissions": ["document.read"]}]}
```

**Go**

```go
res, err := client.CheckDetailed(ctx, permio.CheckRequest{
    Principal:   "alice",
    Resources:   []string{"/documents/42", "/invoices/1"},
    Permissions: []string{"document.read"},
})
// handle err
res.Allowed // false
res.Missing // [{Resource: "/invoices/1", Permissions: ["document.read"]}]
```

**Python**

```python
result = permio.check_detailed("alice", "document.read", ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"])
result.allowed  # False
result.missing  # [MissingPermission(resource="/invoices/1", permissions=["document.read"])]
```

`check()` returns just the `bool`. See [Checking permissions](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#checking-permissions).

**Rust**

```rust
use permio::Check;

let result = permio
    .check_detailed(
        Check::new("alice")
            .resources(["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"])
            .permission("document.read"),
    )
    .await?;
println!("{} {:?}", result.allowed, result.missing);
```

`permio.check("alice", "document.read", "/documents/42")` returns just the `bool`. See
[Checking permissions](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/#checking-permissions).

**Java**

```java
import io.perms.CheckResult;
import java.util.List;

CheckResult result = permio.checkDetailed(
    "alice", List.of("document.read"), List.of("/documents/42", "/invoices/1"));
result.allowed(); // false
result.missing(); // [MissingPermission{resource=/invoices/1, permissions=[document.read]}]
```

`check` returns just the boolean. See [Checking permissions](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/#checking-permissions).

### BatchCheck

`POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/check/batch`

Checks a principal's permissions on each resource **separately** and returns one result per resource, in request
order. It is evaluated exactly like [Check](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#check): inheritance, stored `_` wildcards, roles and the principal's
[groups](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/) all count, and it fails closed. A resource is allowed only if the principal holds
**every** requested permission on it.

**Needs:** the same as Check: `permission.check` on every resource and on the principal.

**Request** (`BatchCheckRequest`)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. Project to check in. |
| `principal_id` | string | Required. The principal being checked. |
| `resource_uris` | string[] | Required. 1–100 unique resource URIs, with the same rules as Check. |
| `permissions` | string[] | Required. 1–100 unique permission names. |

**Response** (`BatchCheckResponse`)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | BatchCheckResult[] | One per requested resource, in request order. |

**BatchCheckResult**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource_uri` | string | The resource. |
| `allowed` | bool | `true` if the principal holds every requested permission on it. |
| `missing_permissions` | string[] | The requested permissions not held on it, in request order. |

**Errors:** `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a malformed request; `PERMISSION_DENIED` if the API key lacks `permission.check`;
`NOT_FOUND` if `principal_id` is `group:<slug>` and that group doesn't exist.

**TypeScript**

```ts
const allowed = await permio.batchCheck({
  principal: "alice",
  resources: ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"],
  permission: "document.read",
});
allowed.get("/documents/42"); // true
```

Available from SDK 0.2.0. `batchCheckDetailed` returns the missing permissions too. See
[Batch checks](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/typescript/#batch-checks).

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/check/batch" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "project_name": "default",
    "principal_id": "alice",
    "resource_uris": ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"],
    "permissions": ["document.read"]
  }'
```

```json
{"results": [
  {"resourceUri": "/documents/42", "allowed": true},
  {"resourceUri": "/invoices/1", "missingPermissions": ["document.read"]}
]}
```

**Go**

```go
allowed, err := client.BatchCheck(ctx, "alice",
    []string{"document.read"},
    []string{"/documents/42", "/invoices/1"})
// handle err
allowed["/documents/42"] // true
```

`BatchCheckDetailed` returns the missing permissions too. See [Batch checks](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/go/#batch-checks).

**Python**

```python
allowed = permio.batch_check("alice", "document.read", ["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"])
allowed["/documents/42"]  # True
```

`batch_check_detailed` returns the missing permissions too. See [Batch checks](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#batch-checks).

**Rust**

```rust
use permio::BatchCheck;

let entries = permio
    .batch_check(
        BatchCheck::new("alice")
            .resources(["/documents/42", "/invoices/1"])
            .permission("document.read"),
    )
    .await?;
for e in &entries {
    println!("{} {} {:?}", e.resource, e.allowed, e.missing);
}
```

More than 100 resources are split into concurrent calls. See [`batch_check`](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/#batch_check).

**Java**

```java
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

Map<String, Boolean> allowed =
    permio.batchCheck("alice", "document.read", List.of("/documents/42", "/invoices/1"));
allowed.get("/documents/42"); // true
```

`batchCheckDetailed` returns the missing permissions too. See [Batch checks](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/#batch-checks).

The Go, Python, Rust and Java examples on this page use a client set up as in [Clients](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/#clients).

### Permissions

#### CreatePermission

`POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions`

Creates a permission. This call is idempotent: if the permission already exists, it is updated. Returns the
`Permission`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. |
| `name` | string | Required. |
| `description` | string | Optional. |

**TypeScript**

```ts
const perm = await permio.permissions.createPermission({
  projectName: "default",
  name: "document.read",
  description: "Read documents",
});
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "name": "document.read", "description": "Read documents"}'
```

**Go**

```go
perm, err := client.CreatePermission(ctx, "document.read", "Read documents")
```

If the permission already exists with another description, the SDK returns an error of kind `KindAlreadyExists`;
use `UpdatePermission` to change it.

**Python**

The SDK has no helper for this RPC, so call it through the raw client:

```python
from permio import raw

perm = permio.permissions.CreatePermission(
    raw.permissions_pb2.CreatePermissionRequest(
        project_name="default", name="document.read", description="Read documents"
    )
)
```

**Rust**

There is no helper for this RPC; use the raw client.

```rust
use permio::raw::permissions::v1::CreatePermissionRequest;

let perm = permio
    .raw_permissions()
    .create_permission(CreatePermissionRequest {
        project_name: "default".into(),
        name: "document.read".into(),
        description: "Read documents".into(),
    })
    .await?
    .into_inner();
```

**Java**

The SDK has no helper for this RPC, so use the generated stub from `permio.raw()`. It sends the API key and applies
the client's timeout, but not its default project: set `project_name` yourself. See
[Raw client](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/java/#raw-client).

```java
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.CreatePermissionRequest;
import io.perms.proto.permissions.v1.Permission;

Permission perm = permio.raw().permissions().createPermission(
    CreatePermissionRequest.newBuilder()
        .setProjectName("default")
        .setName("document.read")
        .setDescription("Read documents")
        .build());
```

#### GetPermission

`GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/{name}?project_name=…`

Returns a `Permission` by name, or `NOT_FOUND`.

**TypeScript**

```ts
const perm = await permio.permissions.getPermission({ projectName: "default", name: "document.read" });
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/document.read?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

#### UpdatePermission

`PUT /permissions-service/v1/permissions/{name}`

Updates a permission, or returns `NOT_FOUND` if it doesn't exist. Returns the updated `Permission`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. |
| `name` | string | Required (path). The current name. |
| `new_name` | string | Optional. A new name; if omitted, the name stays the same. |
| `description` | string | The new description. |

**TypeScript**

```ts
await permio.permissions.updatePermission({
  projectName: "default",
  name: "document.read",
  description: "Read any document",
});
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X PUT "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/document.read" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "description": "Read any document"}'
```

#### DeletePermission

`DELETE /permissions-service/v1/permissions/{name}?project_name=…`

Deletes a permission. This call is idempotent: it succeeds whether or not the permission existed.

**TypeScript**

```ts
await permio.permissions.deletePermission({ projectName: "default", name: "document.read" });
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X DELETE "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/document.read?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

#### ListPermissions

`GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions?project_name=…`

Lists permissions in a project. The response has `permissions` (Permission[]) and `pagination`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. |
| `pagination` | [PaginationRequest](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/pagination/) | Optional. `limit` (1–100) and `cursor`. |
| `search` | string | Optional. Filters by name. |

**TypeScript**

```ts
for await (const p of permio.listPermissions({ search: "document." })) {
  console.log(p.name);
}
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions?project_name=default&search=document.&pagination.limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

### Roles

#### CreateRole

`POST /permissions-service/v1/roles`

Creates a role from existing permissions. This call is idempotent: if the role already exists, it is updated.
Returns the `Role`, including its `id`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. |
| `name` | string | Required. |
| `description` | string | Optional. |
| `permissions` | string[] | Permission **names**, e.g. `["document.read"]`. |

**TypeScript**

```ts
const role = await permio.permissions.createRole({
  projectName: "default",
  name: "viewer",
  description: "Can read documents",
  permissions: ["document.read"],
});
console.log(role.id);
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/roles" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "name": "viewer", "description": "Can read documents", "permissions": ["document.read"]}'
```

#### GetRole

`GET /permissions-service/v1/roles/{id}?project_name=…`

Returns a `Role` by ID.

**TypeScript**

```ts
const role = await permio.permissions.getRole({ projectName: "default", id: roleId });
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/roles/ROLE_ID?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

#### UpdateRole

`PUT /permissions-service/v1/roles/{id}`

Replaces a role's name, description and permissions, or returns `NOT_FOUND`. Returns the updated `Role`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. |
| `id` | string | Required (path). |
| `name` | string | Required. |
| `description` | string | Optional. |
| `permissions` | string[] | Permission names. |

**TypeScript**

```ts
await permio.permissions.updateRole({
  projectName: "default",
  id: roleId,
  name: "editor",
  permissions: ["document.read", "document.write"],
});
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X PUT "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/roles/ROLE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "name": "editor", "permissions": ["document.read", "document.write"]}'
```

#### DeleteRole

`DELETE /permissions-service/v1/roles/{id}?project_name=…`

Deletes a role. This call is idempotent.

**TypeScript**

```ts
await permio.permissions.deleteRole({ projectName: "default", id: roleId });
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X DELETE "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/roles/ROLE_ID?project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

#### ListRoles

`GET /permissions-service/v1/roles?project_name=…`

Lists roles in a project. The response has `roles` (Role[]) and `pagination`. It takes the same `pagination` and
`search` fields as [ListPermissions](https://docs.perms.io/api-reference/permissions/#listpermissions).

**TypeScript**

```ts
for await (const role of permio.listRoles()) {
  console.log(role.id, role.name);
}
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/roles?project_name=default&pagination.limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

### Grants

#### GrantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource

`POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/assign`

Grants permissions and/or roles to a principal on a resource. Grants are additive: existing grants are kept. The
grant also applies to every resource beneath `resource_uri`. Unknown permissions or roles are rejected with
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

To grant to a [group](https://docs.perms.io/concepts/groups/), set `user_id` to `group:<slug>`. The group must exist in the project,
or the call fails with `NOT_FOUND`. Every member of the group then holds the grant. Grants to groups don't count
towards your unique principals.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_name` | string | Required. |
| `user_id` | string | Required. The principal ID, the same value you pass as `principal_id` to Check. |
| `resource_uri` | string | Required. |
| `permissions` | string[] | Permission **names**. |
| `roles` | string[] | Role **IDs**. |

**TypeScript**

```ts
await permio.permissions.grantUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource({
  projectName: "default",
  userId: "alice",
  resourceUri: "/documents",
  roles: [roleId],
});
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/assign" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "user_id": "alice", "resource_uri": "/documents", "roles": ["ROLE_ID"]}'
```

**Go**

```go
err := client.Grant(ctx, permio.GrantRequest{
    Principal: "alice",
    Resource:  "/documents",
    Roles:     []string{roleID},
})
```

**Python**

```python
permio.grant("alice", "/documents", roles="ROLE_ID")
```

`permissions=` and `roles=` each take one value or a list. See
[Granting and revoking](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/python/#granting-and-revoking).

**Rust**

```rust
use permio::Grant;

permio
    .grant(Grant::new("alice", "/documents").role("ROLE_ID"))
    .await?;
```

Add `.permission("document.read")` to grant permissions by name. See
[Granting and revoking](https://docs.perms.io/sdk/rust/#granting-and-revoking).

**Java**

```java
import io.perms.Grant;

permio.grant(Grant.to("alice").on("/documents").roles("ROLE_ID"));
```

The client's project is used. Grants are never retried automatically.

#### RevokeUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource

`POST /permissions-service/v1/permissions/revoke`

Removes permissions and/or roles from a principal on a resource. It takes the same fields as Grant. Revoking from a
`group:<slug>` principal works even if the group no longer exists, so stray grants can be cleaned up.

**TypeScript**

```ts
await permio.permissions.revokeUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource({
  projectName: "default",
  userId: "alice",
  resourceUri: "/documents",
  roles: [roleId],
});
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl -X POST "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/revoke" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_name": "default", "user_id": "alice", "resource_uri": "/documents", "roles": ["ROLE_ID"]}'
```

**Go**

```go
err := client.Revoke(ctx, permio.GrantRequest{
    Principal: "alice",
    Resource:  "/documents",
    Roles:     []string{roleID},
})
```

**Python**

```python
permio.revoke("alice", "/documents", roles="ROLE_ID")
```

**Rust**

```rust
use permio::Grant;

permio
    .revoke(Grant::new("alice", "/documents").role("ROLE_ID"))
    .await?;
```

**Java**

```java
import io.perms.Grant;

permio.revoke(Grant.to("alice").on("/documents").roles("ROLE_ID"));
```

#### GetUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource

`GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/user/{user_id}/resource/{resource_uri=**}?project_name=…`
`GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/user/{user_id}/resource?resource_uri=…&project_name=…`

Returns the permissions and roles assigned to a principal on one resource. The response has `project_name`,
`user_id`, `resource_uri`, `permissions` (names) and `roles` (IDs).

In the first form, send the resource URI **without** its leading slash. The second form passes the URI exactly as a
query parameter.

**TypeScript**

```ts
const res = await permio.permissions.getUserPermissionsAndRolesOnResource({
  projectName: "default",
  userId: "alice",
  resourceUri: "/documents",
});
```

**cURL**

```bash
curl "$PERMIO_API/permissions-service/v1/permissions/user/alice/resource?resource_uri=/documents&project_name=default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

#### ListPrincipals

`GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/principals?project_name=…`

Lists the IDs of principals with grants in the project. The response has `principals` (string[]) and `pagination`.
It takes `pagination` and `search`.

**TypeScript**


**cURL**

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERMIO_API_KEY"
```

#### GetAllAssignmentsForPrincipal

`GET /permissions-service/v1/permissions/assignments/principal/{principal_id=**}?project_name=…`

Lists every grant a principal has in the project. The response has `assignments` (Assignment[]) and `pagination`.
Principal IDs may contain slashes.

**TypeScript**

```ts
for await (const a of permio.listAssignments({ principal: "alice" })) {
  console.log(a.resourceUri, a.permissions.map((p) => p.name), a.roles.map((r) => r.name));
}
```
